definition_zh: 巨大的；极大的；极好的；了不起的
definition_en: extremely great in size, amount, or effect, or extremely good
core_image: 一面山壁横在眼前，仰头看到脖颈发酸才见顶
scene: 站在峡谷边抬头，两壁高得让人后退半步，风从下面直往上冲。 The canyon drops a tremendous distance to the river.
sceneCN: 这里 tremendous 是「巨大的」（第 1 个义项：体积、数量或影响极大）；句意为峡谷到河面的落差极大。仰头看不清顶的山壁正是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 形容词：极好的；了不起的

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「极大地；非常」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「巨大」
同根名词，义为「震动；颤栗」

senses.title: Extremely great in size
senses.definition: very great in size, extent, or degree
senses.definitionCN: 在体积、范围或程度上非常大
senses.example: They crossed a tremendous desert.
senses.exampleCN: 他们穿过一片巨大的沙漠。
senses.why: A thing so great that one trembles at it is simply great in size, which is the direct descendant.
senses.whyCN: 大到让人发抖之物，直接就成了「体积巨大」，这是最直接的后代义。

senses.title: Extremely great in amount
senses.definition: very large in number or quantity
senses.definitionCN: 在数量上很大
senses.example: A tremendous number of people came.
senses.exampleCN: 来了极多的人。
senses.why: Number is only size counted, so the same adjective moves from space to quantity.
senses.whyCN: 数量不过是数出来的体积，所以同一个形容词从空间挪到数目上。

senses.title: Extremely strong in force
senses.definition: very strong in effect or force
senses.definitionCN: 在效力或影响上非常强
senses.example: The plan met tremendous opposition.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划遭到极大的反对。
senses.why: Force that makes people tremble is the sense closest to the Latin, applied to effect rather than body.
senses.whyCN: 让人发抖的力量最接近拉丁原义，只是作用在效果而非身体上。

senses.title: Extremely good
senses.definition: excellent or wonderful, in everyday approval
senses.definitionCN: 在日常赞许中表示「很棒」
senses.example: We had a tremendous time.
senses.exampleCN: 我们玩得非常开心。
senses.why: Weakened further, the awe becomes everyday praise for something excellent.
senses.whyCN: 再弱化一步，那份敬畏就变成对好东西的日常夸赞。

senses.title: Arousing awe or dread
senses.definition: so great as to cause wonder or fear, the oldest sense
senses.definitionCN: 大到令人惊叹或畏惧，这是最古老的义项
senses.example: The storm came on with tremendous force,
senses.exampleCN: 风暴以令人畏惧的力量袭来。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: tremendus names what must be trembled at.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：tremendus 指的就是「必须对它发抖」之物。

intro.en: The word is Latin tremendus, to be trembled at, from tremere, to tremble.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语 tremendus，意为「令人发抖的」，出自动词 tremere（发抖）。

items.en: Tremere means to tremble, and tremendus is the thing one must tremble at.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tremere 意为发抖，tremendus 就是「必须对它发抖」之物。

items.en: The Latin gerundive ending -ndus marks something that ought to be feared or done.
items.cn: 拉丁动形词词尾 -ndus 标记「应该被畏惧或应做」之物。

items.en: English first uses the word for things that inspire awe and dread.
items.cn: 英语最初用这个词指引起敬畏与恐惧的事物。

items.en: In the nineteenth century it weakens into a general word for very great.
items.cn: 十九世纪它弱化为泛指「非常大」的词。

items.en: Recent usage adds an everyday sense of very good.
items.cn: 近期用法又添上「非常好」的日常义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the trem- root of trembling, while the near-meaning group gathers other words for very large.
note.cn: 形近组共用 trem-（发抖）词根，近义组汇集表示极大的其他词。

entries.definition: to shake slightly
a slight shaking
shaking, or timid
to a very great degree
very large indeed
extremely large
extremely wide in area
as large as a giant statue

normalIntro.en: The word contains tremble, and it once meant something that made you tremble.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词里含着 tremble，它原先指让人发抖的东西。

normal.en: Tremere is to tremble, so tremendous means to be trembled at.
normal.cn: tremere 是发抖，所以 tremendous 就是「令人发抖的」。

normal.en: Over time the trembling became mere size, and the word now means very great.
normal.cn: 久而久之，那份颤抖只剩下「大」，如今意为极大。

normal.en: Tremor and tremulous share the same root, so they are one family.
normal.cn: tremor 与 tremulous 同根，属于一个家族。

normal.en: The adverb tremendously means to a great degree.
normal.cn: 副词 tremendously 意为「极大地」。

normal.en: In speech it also means very good, as in a tremendous day.
normal.cn: 口语里也表示很好，如 a tremendous day。

abstract.en: Picture a cliff so high that your neck aches to see the top.
abstract.cn: 想象一面山壁高到抬头看到脖子酸。

abstract.en: Feel the small tremble in your legs at the edge.
abstract.cn: 感受站在边沿时腿上的那阵轻颤。

abstract.en: Then let the same shake become praise for a good meal.
abstract.cn: 再让这阵颤动变成对一顿好饭的称赞。

examples.en: The project required a tremendous amount of work.
examples.cn: 这个项目需要大量的工作。

examples.en: She felt tremendous pressure before the exam.
examples.cn: 考试前她感到巨大的压力。

examples.en: You did a tremendous job on the report.
examples.cn: 这份报告你做得非常出色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「穿门得死」——门大得要穿过去都累死，真是巨大。

root: 拉丁语 tremere（发抖）的动形词 tremendus（令人发抖的）；同族有 tremble、tremor、tremulous

sensesIntro.en: All senses descend from awe: something so great that a person trembles at it.
sensesIntro.cn: 所有义项都源自敬畏：某物大到让人发抖。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cliff so high the neck aches.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面高到脖子发酸的山壁。

branches.en: The size and number senses, the plain modern use.
branches.cn: 体积与数量义：现代最普通的用法。

branches.en: The force sense, where the effect is overwhelming.
branches.cn: 力量义：影响压倒一切。

branches.en: The praise sense, borrowed from admiring talk.
branches.cn: 赞扬义：从赞赏的话里借来。

branches.en: The awe sense, the oldest and most literal.
branches.cn: 敬畏义：最古老也最字面。

branches.en: The cliff sense, the plain picture of size.
branches.cn: 峭壁义：体积最朴素的画面。

intro.en: The adjective is a Latin gerundive, a form that marks what ought to be feared or done.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是拉丁动形词，这种形式标记「应被畏惧或应做的事」。

latinIntro.en: The trem- stem gives tremble, tremor, tremulous, and tremendous.
latinIntro.cn: trem- 词干生出 tremble、tremor、tremulous 与 tremendous。

items.example: The stem gives tremor and tremble.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干生出 tremor 与 tremble。

items.example: Tremendus is the source of tremendous.
items.exampleCN: tremendus 是 tremendous 的来源。

items.example: Even the suffix -ous survives in tremendous.
items.exampleCN: 连 -ous 这个形容词词尾都留在 tremendous 里。

items.example: A tremor ran through the floor.

items.meaning: to be trembled at, hence huge
items.example: A tremendous wave hit the wall.
The tremendousness of the task scared them.
items.exampleCN: 任务的巨大让他们害怕。

definition_zh: 反对；抵抗；在野阵营；对立立场；对比；天体冲；对手；正式异议
definition_en: the act of resisting or arguing against something, or the side that stands against another
core_image: 两排人隔着一条长桌，一边推、一边挡，桌面中线谁都不肯越过
scene: 会场里两排座位面对面，提案刚念完，前排就有人站起来反驳。 The new road plan ran into strong opposition from residents.
sceneCN: 会场里两排座位面对面，提案刚念完，前排就有人站起来反驳；句中的这个词指「来自某群人的抵抗」（第 1 个义项：对某项计划或政策表示反对并设法阻止）。图中可辨识物件：长桌、两排座椅、摊开的提案、举起的手、麦克风；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 反对；抵抗；对立的一方（不可数或可数）

derivatives.zh: 反对；抵抗
相反的；在……对面
对手；反对者
对立的；反对的

senses.title: Resistance to a plan
senses.definition: active disagreement with a proposal, shown by argument, voting or protest
senses.definitionCN: 对某项提议的积极不同意，通过争辩、投票或抗议表现出来
senses.example: Plans for the tower met fierce opposition at the first hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 建塔方案在第一次听证会上遭到激烈反对。
senses.why: The word is built from 'place against': something is set face to face with a plan and pushes back.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由「放到对面」构成：某样东西被摆到计划对面，然后往回推。

senses.title: The side out of office
senses.definition: the parties or politicians who do not hold government and argue against those who do
senses.definitionCN: 不掌握政府、专门与掌权者争辩的政党或政治人物
senses.example: The opposition voted against the budget in every committee.
senses.exampleCN: 在野阵营在每个委员会都投票反对这份预算。
senses.why: Parliament seats face each other, so the side without power is literally placed opposite the ministers.
senses.whyCN: 议会席位两两相对，于是没有权力的那一边字面上就被安置在部长们的对面。

senses.title: An opposing stance in debate
senses.definition: the position of the speaker or team that argues against the motion
senses.definitionCN: 在辩论中主张反对该项动议的一方所持的立场
senses.example: The debate split into support and opposition before the first recess.
senses.exampleCN: 辩论在第一次休息前就分成了支持与反对两方。
senses.why: A debate is a physical arrangement of voices: one side proposes, the other side is placed against it.
senses.whyCN: 辩论就是声音的排布：一边提出，另一边被安置在它的对面。

senses.title: Contrast or difference
senses.definition: a sharp difference between two things that are set side by side for comparison
senses.definitionCN: 两样东西并置比较时显现的鲜明差异
senses.example: The opposition between the two theories is sharper than it looks.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种理论之间的对立比表面上更尖锐。
senses.why: Two things placed opposite each other define their difference by their facing positions.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西相对摆放，正是靠面对面的位置显出彼此的差异。

senses.title: Astronomical opposition
senses.titleCN: 天体冲（行星与太阳相对）
senses.definition: the position in which a planet is on the opposite side of Earth from the sun
senses.definitionCN: 某颗行星位于地球与太阳相对一侧的位置
senses.example: Mars reaches opposition roughly every two years.
senses.exampleCN: 火星大约每两年到达一次冲的位置。
senses.why: In the sky the same geometry works: two bodies sit on opposite sides of the observer and face each other.
senses.whyCN: 天空里也是同一套几何：两个天体位于观测者的两侧，彼此相对。

senses.title: The opposing team
senses.definition: the team or player that one is competing against in a match
senses.definitionCN: 比赛中与之竞争的那支队伍或那名选手
senses.example: The home side beat the opposition by three goals.
senses.exampleCN: 主队以三球击败对手。
senses.why: A match places two teams on opposite halves of the field, and the other half is simply the opposition.
senses.whyCN: 一场比赛把两支队伍放在球场的两个半场，另一半就是「对面」。

senses.title: Structural opposition
senses.definition: a relation between two elements that are defined by being different from each other
senses.definitionCN: 两个要素因彼此不同而互相界定所形成的关系
senses.example: The linguist studied the opposition between voiced and voiceless sounds.
senses.exampleCN: 这位语言学家研究浊音与清音之间的对立。
senses.why: In a system, meaning can come from position: each item is what the item opposite it is not.
senses.whyCN: 在一个系统里，意义可以来自位置：每一项就是它对那一项所不是的东西。

senses.title: A formal objection
senses.definition: a written or official statement asking a court or authority to refuse something
senses.definitionCN: 请求法院或主管机关拒绝某项事项的书面或正式陈述
senses.example: The lawyers filed a formal opposition to the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 律师们就这项合并提交了正式的反对意见。
senses.why: The physical act of standing against becomes a document that is placed against a request.
senses.whyCN: 「站到对面」这个动作变成了一份文件，被摆到某项申请的对立面。

intro.en: Opposition comes from Latin oppositio, a noun from opponere 'to place against', whose past participle is oppositus. The astronomical and political senses are later extensions of the same geometry. The exact first date in English is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个词出自拉丁语中意为「放到对面」的动词，其过去分词意为「被放到对面的」，相应的名词意为「对立、反对」。天文义与政治义都是同一套位置关系在后来的延伸。它在英语中首见的确切年代不确定。

items.en: Ponere meant 'to place, to put'. Its participle positus gave position, posit and deposit.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为「放置、安放」。它的分词形式给了「位置」「假定」「存放」等英语词。

items.en: Ob- 'against' plus ponere produced opponere 'to place in the way, to set against'. The prefix is assimilated to op- before p.
items.cn: 意为「对着」的前缀加「放置」构成这个动词，表示「挡在路上、放到对面」。前缀在唇音前同化为「欧普」的形式。

items.en: The past participle oppositus meant 'placed against, set opposite'. English opposite comes from the same participle.
items.cn: 这个过去分词意为「被放到对面的、相对的」。英语的「相反的、对面的」就出自同一分词。

items.en: The noun oppositio named the act of placing against, and later the state of being opposed.
items.cn: 相应的名词指「放到对面的动作」，后来也指「彼此相对的状态」。

items.en: Old French carried the noun toward English in the fourteenth century, still with the sense of a position facing another.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词带向英语，时间约在十四世纪，当时仍指「面对另一方的位置」。

items.en: The parliamentary sense is generally dated to the eighteenth century and the astronomical one is older in Latin; both are best described as extensions rather than separate words.
items.cn: 议会义一般认为定于十八世纪，天文义在拉丁语中更早；两者都应视为同一词的延伸，而非另立新词。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin 'place against' root or a very close spelling; the second group gathers words for resisting, objecting and competing.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「放到对面」的词根，或拼写极近；第二组汇集了表示抵抗、反对与竞争的词。

entries.definition: Facing something, or completely different from it. It describes a position or a quality, not an organized campaign of resistance.
entries.definitionCN: 指面对某物，或与某物完全不同。它描述位置或性质，不指有组织的抵抗行动。

entries.definition: To argue or vote against something. It is the action; the noun names the action or the side that performs it.
entries.definitionCN: 指以言辞或投票反对某事。它是动作本身；名词则指这个动作或采取动作的一方。

entries.definition: A person who is against you in a contest or an argument. It names a rival, not the resistance as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指在竞赛或争论中与你相对的人。它指对手，不指整体的抵抗。

entries.definition: Characterized by being against something. It describes a tendency or a style, while the noun names the thing itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指具有反对特征的。它描述一种倾向或风格，而名词指事物本身。

entries.definition: The act of pushing back, often with force or endurance. It stresses holding one's ground more than stating a case.
entries.definitionCN: 指往回推的行为，常带力量或持久性。它更强调守住阵地，而不是陈述理由。

entries.definition: A reason given for disagreeing, often in a meeting or a court. It is one spoken item, not a whole side.
entries.definitionCN: 指为表示不同意而给出的理由，常出现在会议或法庭上。它是一条说出口的意见，不是一整方。

entries.definition: Disagreement with an authority or an accepted view, often on principle. It can be quiet and individual.
entries.definitionCN: 指对权威或公认看法的不认同，常出于原则。它可以是安静的、个人的。

entries.definition: A continuing contest between two sides for the same prize. It is about winning, not about blocking a proposal.
entries.definitionCN: 指两方为同一目标持续竞争。它关乎胜负，而不是阻止某项提议。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin picture of placing one thing against another, the derived family, and the fixed phrases of parliaments and matches.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：把一样东西放到另一样对面的拉丁画面、派生词族，以及议会与赛场的固定搭配。

normal.en: The prefix means 'against', the root means 'place': the whole word is a placing against.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「对着」，词根意为「放」：整个词就是「放到对面」。

normal.en: Parliament seats face each other, so the side without power is called the opposition.
normal.cn: 议会席位两两相对，所以没有权力的那一边就被称为反对方。

normal.en: A match puts two teams on opposite halves: the other half is the opposition.
normal.cn: 比赛把两队放在两个半场：另一半就是对手。

normal.en: The family runs oppose, opposite, opponent and oppositional.
normal.cn: 同族词包括反对、相反的、对手与对立的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: meet strong opposition, in opposition to, the official opposition.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：遭到强烈反对、与……相对、官方反对党。

abstract.en: Picture two chairs dragged to face each other; whatever sits on one chair is defined by the other.
abstract.cn: 想象两把椅子被拖到彼此对面；坐在其中一把上的东西，由另一把来界定。

abstract.en: Opposition is not hatred; it is geometry. The other side is simply the side that faces yours.
abstract.cn: 反对不是仇恨，而是几何：另一边只是与你这一边相对的那一边。

abstract.en: The same geometry explains a debate, a lawsuit, a planet in the sky and a rival team.
abstract.cn: 同一套几何能解释一场辩论、一桩诉讼、天上的一颗行星和一支对手球队。

examples.en: Opposition to the new runway grew after the noise reports were published.
examples.cn: 噪音报告公布后，反对新建跑道的声音变大了。

examples.en: The opposition walked out when the minister refused to answer.
examples.cn: 部长拒绝回答时，反对党阵营退场了。

examples.en: In this system every sound is defined by its opposition to another sound.
examples.cn: 在这个系统里，每个音都由它与另一个音的对立来界定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧波季申」——「欧」的一边「波」到对面，另一边就「季申」申辩，正好是两方对着站

root: 拉丁 opponere「放到对面」（ob-「对着」+ ponere「放」）的过去分词 oppositus，名词 oppositio；同根词包括表示「反对」的动词、表示「对面」的形容词与表示「对手」的名词，以及同出「放置」词根的位置、组合二词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from one arrangement: two things are placed face to face, and that facing becomes resistance, a rival side, a contrast, a planet in line, or a filed objection.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从一种摆法出发：两样东西被放到面对面，这种相对就变成抵抗、对立的一方、差异、排成一线的一颗行星，或一份提交的异议。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: place one thing against another and let each define the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：把一样东西放到另一样对面，让彼此互相界定。

branches.en: RESIST AND FILE: one pushes back in the street or the hearing, the other puts the refusal into an official document.
branches.cn: 抵抗与备案：一个在街头或听证会上往回推，另一个把拒绝写成正式文件。

branches.en: RIVAL SIDES: the party out of office and the team on the other half both occupy the facing position.
branches.cn: 互为对手的两方：在野阵营与另一个半场的球队，都占据着面对面的位置。

branches.en: STANCE AND DIFFERENCE: in a debate one takes a side; between two things the side becomes a visible contrast.
branches.cn: 立场与差异：在辩论中选一边；在两样东西之间，这一边就变成可见的对比。

branches.en: CELESTIAL LINE: a planet, the earth and the sun fall into the same facing arrangement.
branches.cn: 天上的连线：行星、地球与太阳排成同一套相对的位置。

branches.en: STRUCTURED PAIR: inside a system, each element is what the element opposite it is not.
branches.cn: 结构中的成对：在一个系统里，每个要素就是与它相对的那个要素所不是的东西。

intro.en: Opposition is built from a Latin prefix meaning 'against', a Latin root meaning 'place', and a Latin noun suffix.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个意为「对着」的拉丁前缀、一个意为「放」的拉丁词根和一个拉丁名词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere 'to place' supplies the root; ob- 'against' supplies direction; -io, -ionem turns the participle into a noun of action.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中意为「放」的动词提供词根；意为「对着」的前缀提供方向；名词后缀把分词变成表示动作的名词。

items.structure: ob- (Latin prefix, 'against, in the way of'; assimilated to op- before p)
items.meaningCN: 对着；迎面，语义偏移为「反对」
items.example: The prefix puts the action in someone's way.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作挡在某人路上。

items.example: The root appears in compose and position.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根出现在「组成」与「位置」里。

items.meaningCN: 把自己放到对面，语义偏移为「反对、抵抗」
items.exampleCN: 几名成员反对这项动议。

items.meaningCN: 被放到对面的，语义偏移为「相反的、对面的」
items.example: The bank is opposite the station.

items.meaning: the act or state of being against
items.meaningCN: 处于对面的动作或状态，语义偏移为「反对、反对派」
items.example: The plan met opposition at once.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划立刻遭到反对。

items.structure: op- + ponent (Latin ponens, present participle of ponere)
items.meaningCN: 把自己放到对面的人，语义偏移为「对手、反对者」
items.example: Her opponent withdrew before the final.
items.exampleCN: 她的对手在决赛前退出了。

items.meaningCN: 具有反对性质的，语义偏移为「对立的」
items.example: The party adopted an oppositional tone.
items.exampleCN: 该党采取了对抗性的语气。

items.meaningCN: 放到一起，语义偏移为「组成、创作」
items.exampleCN: 十名成员组成这个委员会。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 放到对面；被放到对面的

definition_zh: 工资；工钱；报酬；发动（战争、运动等）
definition_en: money paid regularly for work, usually by the hour or day; to start and carry on a war or campaign
core_image: 掌心里数好的钱：干一天活，换一天的钱
scene: 面包房打烊，老板从围裙口袋里掏出小信封。 The workers demanded a fair wage for their extra hours.
sceneCN: 这里 wage 是「工资」（第 1 个义项：按时间计的劳动报酬）；句意是工人们要求额外工时获得公平的报酬。

pos.zh: 动词：发动；进行（战争、运动、斗争）

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「赌注」，与 wage 同出一源，指押上的「承诺之物」
名词复数形式，常特指按周或日结算的体力劳动报酬
形容词，义为「领薪水的」，由过去分词转作定语

senses.title: Payment for work by time
senses.titleCN: 工资：按时间计算的劳动报酬
senses.definition: money paid regularly for labor, usually calculated by the hour or day
senses.definitionCN: 按小时或天数定期支付给劳动者的钱
senses.example: The workers demanded a fair wage for their extra hours.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们要求额外的工时获得公平的报酬。
senses.why: Old English wedd meant a pledge; promised payment for a day's work became the wage.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 wedd 意为保证、承诺；为一天劳动承诺的钱就成了工资。

senses.title: Reward or recompense
senses.titleCN: 报酬：行为的报偿或代价
senses.definition: a reward or deserved return for something done, often figurative
senses.definitionCN: 对所做之事的报偿或应得的回报，常用于比喻
senses.example: Peace of mind was the wages of her long patience.
senses.exampleCN: 内心的安宁是她长久耐心的报偿。
senses.why: Whatever is pledged in return for deeds can be paid in more than money.
senses.whyCN: 凡为行为承诺过的回报，可以不止用金钱来支付。

senses.title: To carry on a struggle
senses.titleCN: 发动：开始并进行一场斗争
senses.definition: to start and continue a war, campaign, or organized struggle
senses.definitionCN: 发动并持续进行战争、运动或有组织的斗争
senses.example: The city waged a long campaign against litter.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市发起了一场长期的反垃圾运动。
senses.why: A pledge made to fight becomes the fight itself; the promise turns into action.
senses.whyCN: 为战斗许下的承诺最终成了战斗本身，承诺化为行动。

senses.title: Wages as the income class
senses.titleCN: 工薪：以工资为生的阶层视角
senses.definition: payment for work considered as a class of income, as opposed to salary or profit
senses.definitionCN: 作为收入类别看待的劳动报酬，区别于薪金或利润
senses.example: Wages and prices rose together that decade.
senses.exampleCN: 那十年里工资和物价一同上涨。
senses.why: Counting pay in hours makes it a social category, not just a private sum.
senses.whyCN: 按时计酬使工资成为一种社会类别，而不只是一笔私人钱款。

intro.en: Wage descends through Old North French from Old English and Frankish roots meaning a pledge or surety.
intro.cn: wage 经古北方法语上溯至古英语与法兰克语词根，意为保证、担保。

items.en: The reconstructed root *wadi- means a pledge or security, something handed over as a promise.
items.cn: 重构词根 *wadi- 意为保证、抵押物，即作为承诺而交出的东西。

items.en: Wedd means a pledge or surety; related forms appear across Germanic languages.
items.cn: 古英语 wedd 意为承诺、担保，同源形式见于各日耳曼语。

items.en: The Frankish loan becomes wage in Norman French, meaning a pledge and then payment.
items.cn: 法兰克语借词进入诺曼法语作 wage，先指担保，后指酬金。

items.en: Middle English takes wage as payment pledged for service, especially daily work.
items.cn: 中古英语取 wage 为劳务的应许报酬，尤指按日结算的工钱。

items.en: The verb sense of waging war grows from the pledge to carry a fight through.
items.cn: 15 至 16 世纪，wage 的动词义由「承诺作战到底」发展为「发动战争」。

items.en: Wage now names hourly pay and any sustained campaign, from minimum wage to waging peace.
items.cn: 如今 wage 既指时薪，也指任何持续的行动，从最低工资到发动的运动。

note.en: Wage sits beside its Germanic pledge-family and the pay word-field; look-alikes share the pledge-root, near meanings share the field of reward.
note.cn: wage 与日耳曼「担保」词族及「报酬」义场相邻：形近组共享担保词根，近义组共享报偿义场。

entries.definition: a bet; to bet money on an outcome
entries.definitionCN: 赌注、打赌；与 wage 同出「担保」词根，指押上的承诺

entries.definition: regular payment for work, plural form
entries.definitionCN: 工钱（复数形式）；历史上连带的 -s 曾被误作复数后缀

entries.definition: a piece of wood or metal with a pointed edge for splitting things
entries.definitionCN: 楔子；与 wage 仅一字母之差，词源不同，只是拼写相近

entries.definition: something pledged as a guarantee, especially in old texts
entries.definitionCN: 抵押物、挑战信物；古语用词，与 wage 同源变体

entries.definition: to promise, involve, or hire; to enter into conflict
entries.definitionCN: 使承诺、雇佣、交战；由法语 en- 加 gage（担保）构成

entries.definition: fixed regular payment, usually monthly and for professional work
entries.definitionCN: 薪金；按月固定，多指白领职位的报酬

entries.definition: money received for work, general term
entries.definitionCN: 报酬的总称；不区分结算方式

entries.definition: all money received, from any source
entries.definitionCN: 收入；范围更大，不限于劳动所得

entries.definition: an amount of money paid for something
entries.definitionCN: 付款、款项；指单笔支付而非定期报酬

entries.definition: money paid for a service or a professional's time
entries.definitionCN: 服务费、酬金；按事项或专业服务收取

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the Germanic pledge-family behind wage.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，全部来自 wage 背后的日耳曼「担保」词族。

normal.en: the root means a pledge: a wage is pay promised in advance.
normal.cn: 词根意为担保：wage 是事先承诺好的报酬。

normal.en: wager keeps the same pledge: money staked on a promise.
normal.cn: wager 保留同一担保义：押在承诺上的钱。

normal.en: engage is en- plus gage: bound by a pledge.
normal.cn: engage 是 en- 加 gage：被承诺所约束。

normal.en: wage war grew from the pledge to carry a fight through.
normal.cn: wage war 源于「承诺把战斗打到底」。

normal.en: minimum wage is the fixed phrase everyone meets first.
normal.cn: minimum wage（最低工资）是人人最先遇到的固定搭配。

abstract.en: A hand opens at dusk and coins promised at dawn finally land in it.
abstract.cn: 黄昏摊开的手掌，接住清晨便许下的硬币。

abstract.en: A stamped pledge-paper turns into a small weekly envelope of coins.
abstract.cn: 盖了印的承诺书，变成每周一只装着硬币的小信封。

abstract.en: Promising a fight is already fighting: the pledge marches forward.
abstract.cn: 许诺一战便已在作战：承诺本身向前行进。

examples.en: The factory raised the hourly wage last spring.
examples.cn: 工厂去年春天提高了时薪。

examples.en: They waged a tireless campaign for cleaner rivers.
examples.cn: 他们发起了一场为清洁河流而奋斗的不懈运动。

examples.en: He lives on the wages from two part-time jobs.
examples.cn: 他靠两份兼职的工资生活。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂给」——工钱是雇主「喂给」工人的口粮，一天一喂。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源仍来自日耳曼语的「担保、承诺」。

root: 日耳曼语系词根 *wadi-（保证、抵押）→ 古英语 wedd（承诺、担保）→ 古法兰克语借入诺曼法语 wage（担保→酬金）→ 中古英语 wage。同族词有 wager（赌注）、gage（抵押物）、engage（en- + gage，使受承诺约束）。核心是「为承诺而交出的东西」。

sensesIntro.en: From the pledge outward: promised pay, earned reward, the pledge to fight, and wages as a social income class.
sensesIntro.cn: 从担保向外铺开：承诺的工钱、应得的报偿、作战的承诺，最后到作为社会收入类别的工薪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pledge handed over, first as pay, then as battle joined
core.cn: 核心意象：一份被交出的承诺，先是报酬，后是投入的战斗

branches.en: The root sense: payment pledged for work by the hour
branches.cn: 根本义：按时计酬的承诺报酬

branches.en: Reward beyond money: what deeds deserve
branches.cn: 超出金钱的报偿：行为应得之物

branches.en: Pay counted socially: wages as a class of income
branches.cn: 社会视角的报酬：作为收入类别的工薪

branches.en: The pledge to fight becomes the fight itself
branches.cn: 作战的承诺化为战斗本身

branches.en: Carrying a struggle through, from war to campaigns
branches.cn: 把斗争进行到底，从战争到运动

intro.en: The Germanic pledge-root spreads into English largely through French borrowings of the same Frankish word.
intro.cn: 日耳曼「担保」词根主要通过法语对同一法兰克词的借用进入英语。

latinIntro.en: This family is Germanic rather than Latin; French took it from Frankish speech.
latinIntro.cn: 这一词族属日耳曼而非拉丁来源；法语是从法兰克语中借入它的。

derivatives.zh: 赌注，与 wage 同根的名词
领薪水的，由过去分词转作定语
使承诺、雇佣，由法语 en- 加 gage 构成

definition_zh: 陪审团；评判委员会；评奖团
definition_en: a group of ordinary people chosen to listen to a case and decide it, or a group that decides a competition
core_image: 十二个人坐在木栏后面，低头听完双方发言再做结论
scene: 法庭里空气很闷，旁听席坐满了人，栏杆后那一组人一直在记笔记。 The jury returned after four hours with a clear verdict.
sceneCN: 这里 jury 是「陪审团」（第 1 个义项：依法听审并裁决的一组普通公民），句意为陪审团四小时后回来，给出了明确的裁决。画面里的物件：法庭、木栏、笔记本。

pos.zh: 名词：陪审团；评判委员会；评奖团（集合用法）

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁 jur- 加 -or 构成，指陪审员
由 jur- 加 -ist 构成，指法学家
由 jur- 加 -idical 构成，义为「司法上的」
由 jur- 加 dictio 构成，义为「司法管辖权」

senses.title: A body deciding a court case
senses.definition: a group of citizens sworn to hear evidence and give a verdict in a court
senses.definitionCN: 依法宣誓听取证据并在法庭上作出裁决的一组公民
senses.example: The jury took two days to reach a verdict.
senses.exampleCN: 陪审团用了两天得出结论。
senses.why: The core sense is a sworn body that speaks a verdict for the court.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是向法庭宣告裁决的一个宣誓团体。

senses.title: A panel judging a competition
senses.definition: a group of people chosen to judge a contest and choose winners
senses.definitionCN: 被选出为一比评优劣、决定获奖者的一组人
senses.example: The jury gave the prize to an unknown filmmaker.
senses.exampleCN: 评委会把奖给了一位无名导演。
senses.why: A contest panel judges the way a court does: it weighs and decides.
senses.whyCN: 比赛的评委与法庭一样评判：称量然后决定。

senses.title: Members collectively, with plural agreement
senses.definition: the group treated as a plural body in grammar, so the jury can be said to disagree
senses.definitionCN: 语法上按复数处理，因此可说陪审团意见不一致
senses.example: The jury were still arguing at nine.
senses.exampleCN: 到九点陪审团还在争论。
senses.why: British grammar lets a collective noun take a plural verb when the members act apart.
senses.whyCN: 英式语法允许集合名词在成员各自行动时接复数动词。

senses.title: A temporary makeshift device
senses.definition: a temporary arrangement in nautical or technical use, as a makeshift mast
senses.definitionCN: 航海或技术语境中的临时凑合装置，如临时桅杆
senses.example: They rigged a jury rudder after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后他们装了一副临时舵。
senses.why: Sailors use the word for a thing thrown together to meet an emergency.
senses.whyCN: 水手用这个词指为应付紧急情况匆匆凑成的东西。

senses.title: A body of citizens summoned by law
senses.definition: the body of citizens summoned to serve, seen as an institution
senses.definitionCN: 被依法召集服役的公民群体，作为制度看待
senses.example: Jury service is a duty of the citizen.
senses.exampleCN: 担任陪审员是公民的义务。
senses.why: The institution side names not a case but the standing role of citizens in law.
senses.whyCN: 制度这一面指的不是某个案子，而是公民在法律中的常设角色。

intro.en: Jury comes from Old French juree, an oath, from Latin jurare, to swear, and shares the root jus, law.
intro.cn: jury 来自古法语 juree「誓言」，源自拉丁语 jurare「宣誓」，与 jus「法」同根。

items.en: jurare meant to swear an oath, and jus meant law or right.
items.cn: jurare 意为宣誓，jus 意为法或权利。

items.en: juree named a sworn body of men or the oath they took.
items.cn: juree 指宣誓组成的一群人，或他们所立的誓言。

items.en: English borrowed jury in the fourteenth century as the sworn body in a court.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 jury，指法庭上的宣誓团体。

items.en: The competition sense developed much later, as prizes became contests.
items.cn: 比赛评委义很晚才出现，源于评奖变成竞赛。

items.en: The nautical jury sense is separate and probably from a different source.
items.cn: 航海上的 jury 义是另一回事，很可能来源不同。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin jur- root of law; the near-meaning group holds related bodies and legal roles.
note.cn: 形近组共用拉丁「法」词根 jur-；近义组收相关机构与法律角色。

entries.definition: A member of a jury.
An expert in law.
The authority of a court over a matter.
The decision a jury gives.
A small group chosen to advise or judge.
entries.definitionCN: 指被选出评审或咨询的小组。

entries.definition: A body appointed to judge a special matter.
entries.definitionCN: 较正式，指审理专门事项的裁判机构。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the group to swearing an oath and to the contest panel.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把这个团体连到宣誓，也连到比赛的评委会。

normal.en: Latin jurare, to swear, is the parent of jury.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 jurare「宣誓」是 jury 的亲本。

normal.en: Juror adds -or to the Latin root jur-.
normal.cn: juror 在拉丁词根 jur- 后加 -or。

normal.en: Jury is a collective noun, so a jury can be singular or plural in agreement.
normal.cn: jury 是集合名词，主谓一致可单可复。

normal.en: Grand jury is the American term for a group that decides charges.
normal.cn: grand jury 是美国指决定是否起诉的团体。

normal.en: Jury also judges cakes and films at festivals.
normal.cn: jury 在电影节和比赛里也评判作品。

abstract.en: A jury is twelve ordinary chairs pulled together to decide.
abstract.cn: 陪审团是十二把普通椅子凑在一起做决定。

abstract.en: They swear first and speak after.
abstract.cn: 他们先宣誓，后开口。

abstract.en: A group is trusted where a single voice might lean.
abstract.cn: 一个人可能偏，于是一群人被信任。

examples.en: The jury cleared him of all charges.
examples.cn: 陪审团洗清了他的全部指控。

examples.en: She was called for jury service in March.
examples.cn: 她三月被通知担任陪审员。

examples.en: A jury of five chose the winning film.
examples.cn: 由五人组成的评委会选出了获奖影片。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「主意」—— 十几个人一起拿主意，就是陪审团

root: 拉丁语 jus「法」、jurare「宣誓」→ 古法语 juree「誓言；宣誓的一群人」→ 英语 jury。同族 juror、jurist、jurisdiction。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: a sworn court body, a contest panel, its plural agreement, a nautical makeshift, and the institution of summoned citizens.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：法庭陪审团、比赛评委会、复数一致的用法、航海临时装置，以及被召集公民的制度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a group of ordinary people who swear and then decide.
core.cn: 核心意象：一群普通人先宣誓，再作决定。

branches.en: THE COURTROOM: evidence heard from both sides.
branches.cn: 法庭这条线：听取双方的证据。

branches.en: THE FESTIVAL: films watched and ranked.
branches.cn: 影展这条线：看片并排序。

branches.en: THE LATE ROOM: a group that has not agreed yet.
branches.cn: 深夜评议室这条线：还没取得一致的团体。

branches.en: THE STORM: a rudder lashed together in a hurry.
branches.cn: 风暴这条线：匆匆捆出的临时舵。

branches.en: THE SUMMONS: a letter that makes service a duty.
branches.cn: 传票这条线：一封信把服役变成义务。

intro.en: Jury is borrowed from French and shares the Latin law root jur- with many other words.
intro.cn: jury 从法语借来，与其他许多词共用拉丁「法」词根 jur-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives come from jus and jurare, law and to swear.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词来自 jus 与 jurare，即「法」与「宣誓」。

items.example: The word keeps the oath sense.

definition_zh: 建立；机构；企业；权势集团
definition_en: the act of starting something, or an organization that has been set up
core_image: 一座刚落成的楼房，门口挂上了正式的招牌
scene: 这家小餐馆从一家街边摊发展为当地有名的餐饮机构。 The small restaurant grew from a street stall into a well known local establishment.
sceneCN: 这里 establishment 是「机构；企业」（第 2 个义项：已建立并运作的组织或场所）；句意：这家小餐馆从一家街边摊发展为当地有名的餐饮机构。

pos.zh: 建立；机构；企业；权势集团

derivatives.zh: 建立
已确立的
反建制派的

senses.title: The act of founding
senses.definition: the act of starting an organization or system
senses.definitionCN: 创办组织或制度的行为
senses.example: The establishment of the park took ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 这座公园的建立花了十年。
senses.why: The noun names the action behind the verb establish.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指动词 establish 背后的行为。

senses.title: An organization or business
senses.definition: a company, school or other organized body
senses.definitionCN: 公司、学校或其他有组织的机构
senses.example: The hotel is a family-run establishment.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店是家族经营的机构。
senses.why: Something that has been set up and stands on its own is an establishment.
senses.whyCN: 被设立起来并独立运作的东西，就是一个机构。

senses.title: The ruling group
senses.definition: the powerful people who control a society or field
senses.definitionCN: 控制社会或某一领域的有权势者
senses.example: The young writer challenged the literary establishment.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻作家挑战了文学界的权势集团。
senses.why: The long-established powers are themselves called the establishment.
senses.whyCN: 长期稳固掌权的群体本身就被称为 establishment。

intro.en: Establishment is establish plus -ment, from Latin stabilire, to make stable.
intro.cn: establishment 是 establish 加 -ment，源自拉丁语 stabilire（使稳固）。

items.en: Stabilire means to make stable.
items.cn: stabilire 意为使稳固。

items.en: Establir means to set up.
items.cn: establir 意为设立。

items.en: Establishment names the act of founding.
items.cn: establishment 指建立的行为。

items.en: It also names businesses and institutions.
items.cn: 它也指企业与机构。

items.en: The Establishment means the ruling elite.
items.cn: the Establishment 指掌权的精英集团。

note.en: Establishment is the noun of establish, close to institution and organization.
note.cn: establishment 是 establish 的名词，与机构、组织相近。

entries.definition: to set up
long accepted
against the ruling group
a large organization
a group with a purpose
the building used by a business

normalIntro.en: Establishment is the building left standing after the founding work is done.
normalIntro.cn: establishment 就是创办完成后仍然矗立的那栋建筑。

normal.en: The establishment of a school is its founding.
normal.cn: 学校的 establishment 就是它的创立。

normal.en: A business establishment is a place that does business.
normal.cn: business establishment 是做生意的场所。

normal.en: An educational establishment is a school or college.
normal.cn: educational establishment 指学校或学院。

normal.en: The political establishment means those already in power.
normal.cn: political establishment 指已经掌权的人。

normal.en: Compare institution: an institution is bigger, an establishment can be a single shop.
normal.cn: 对比 institution：institution 更大，establishment 可以只是一家店。

abstract.en: Picture a new sign hanging above a freshly painted door.
abstract.cn: 想象新刷的门上挂起一块新招牌。

abstract.en: Imagine a table where the same powerful people always sit.
abstract.cn: 想象一张总是坐着同一批有权势者的桌子。

abstract.en: Think of roots that have held a tree for a century.
abstract.cn: 想象支撑一棵树百年的根。

examples.en: The establishment of the fund helped many families.
examples.cn: 该基金的建立帮助了许多家庭。

examples.en: This is one of the oldest establishments in town.
examples.cn: 这是城里最古老的机构之一。

examples.en: He became a critic of the cultural establishment.
examples.cn: 他成了文化权势集团的批评者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「establish（建立）＋ ment」——建立起来并一直运作的东西，就是机构；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 stabilire（使稳固）→ establish（建立）＋ -ment → establishment，核心义「被稳固设立起来的事物」。

sensesIntro.en: Establishment first names the founding act, then the organization founded, and finally the long-ruling elite.
sensesIntro.cn: establishment 先指建立行为，再指所建立的机构，最后指长期掌权的精英。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finished building with its official sign in place.
core.cn: 核心意象：落成并挂上正式招牌的建筑。

branches.en: The act of founding is the first sense.
branches.cn: 创立的动作是首要义项。

branches.en: The thing founded becomes an organization.
branches.cn: 被创立的东西成为机构。

branches.en: Long-established power becomes the elite.
branches.cn: 长期稳固的权力变成精英集团。

branches.en: Founding is the first step toward an institution.
branches.cn: 创立是成为机构的第一步。

branches.en: Large institutions make up the establishment.
branches.cn: 大型机构构成权势集团。

intro.en: Establishment adds the noun suffix -ment to establish.
intro.cn: establishment 在 establish 后加名词后缀 -ment。

latinIntro.en: Latin stabilis, firm, stands behind the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stabilis（稳固的）支撑整个词族。

items.exampleCN: established 描述被接受的事物。
anti-establishment 描述对权力的反对。

definition_zh: 疾病；弊病
definition_en: an illness of the body or mind, or a serious problem in a society
core_image: 一片叶子上出现一块褐色斑点，几天后整枝都软了
scene: 叶面上先出现一个褐色小点，几天后整片叶子都软了。 The disease spread through the whole orchard in a month.
sceneCN: 这里 disease 指「疾病」（第 1 个义项：身体或精神的病症）；句意是那种病一个月内传遍了整片果园。

derivatives.zh: 患病的
无病的

senses.title: An illness of the body
senses.definition: an illness that affects the body or mind
senses.definitionCN: 影响身体或精神的病症
senses.example: The disease spread through the orchard.
senses.exampleCN: 那种病传遍了果园。
senses.why: A small spot on one leaf is a whole orchard a month later.
senses.whyCN: 一片叶子上的小点，一个月后就是整片果园。

senses.title: A sickness in society
senses.definition: a serious problem that harms a group or a system
senses.definitionCN: 危害群体或制度的严重问题
senses.example: Greed is a disease of the market.
senses.exampleCN: 贪婪是市场的一种弊病。
senses.why: The same word moves from one body to a body of people.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词从一具身体挪到一群人身上。

intro.en: Disease comes from Old French desaise, a lack of ease, built from des- and aise, comfort.
intro.cn: disease 来自古法语 desaise（不适、不安），由 des-（不）与 aise（安适）构成。

items.en: Adiacens meant lying near, and gave the French word for comfort.
items.cn: adiacens 意为躺卧在旁，后来给出法语里表示安适的词。

items.en: Desaise meant lack of ease or discomfort.
items.cn: 古法语 desaise 指不安适、不舒服。

items.en: English disease first meant unease of any kind.
items.cn: 英语 disease 最初泛指任何不适。

items.en: It narrowed to a named illness of the body.
items.cn: 后来收窄为身体上具体的病症。

items.en: The old sense survives in the idea of a social disease.
items.cn: 旧义在社会弊病这一说法里还留有余影。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on ease, and the meaning group names other words for being unwell.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 ease 构成，近义组列出别的表示身体不适的词。

entries.definition: comfort or freedom from effort
not calm or comfortable
suffering from an illness
the state of being unwell
a feeling of being ill
a small or lasting disorder

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with one brown spot and end with a word for a broken system.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一个褐色斑点开始，落到一个形容坏制度的词。

normal.en: Dis- plus ease: no ease is disease.
normal.cn: dis 加 ease，失去安适就是病。

normal.en: A garden left alone shows disease first on the oldest leaf.
normal.cn: 无人打理的花园，最老的叶子先显出病。

normal.en: Doctors name a disease so that they can fight one thing.
normal.cn: 医生给病取名，才好集中对付一样东西。

normal.en: A disease of the market hides in plain prices.
normal.cn: 市场的弊病藏在平常的价钱里。

normal.en: Clean water is the cheapest guard against disease.
normal.cn: 干净的水是对抗疾病最便宜的守卫。

abstract.en: Picture one brown spot spreading across a leaf.
abstract.cn: 想象一个褐色斑点爬满一片叶子。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp held over a sick branch at night.
abstract.cn: 想象夜里一盏灯照着病枝。

abstract.en: Picture a word moving from a body to a whole town.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词从一具身体挪到整座城。

examples.en: The disease spread through the whole orchard in a month.
examples.cn: 那种病一个月内传遍了整片果园。

examples.en: Clean water prevents many diseases.
examples.cn: 干净的水能预防许多疾病。

examples.en: Greed is a disease of the market.
examples.cn: 贪婪是市场的一种弊病。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disease 记成「不自在」：dis 是不，ease 是安适，身体不安适就是病；一个群体不安适，就是弊病。

root: 来自古法语 desaise（不适），由否定前缀 des- 与 aise（安适）构成，而 aise 可追到拉丁语 adiacens（躺卧在旁）。英语最初泛指各种不适，十六世纪起收窄为具体的病症，后来又引申指社会的弊病。

sensesIntro.en: From a body that has lost its ease to a system that has lost its health.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一具失去安适的身体，到一个失去健康的制度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one brown spot on a leaf, and the whole orchard going soft.
core.cn: 核心意象：叶上一个褐色斑点，整片果园慢慢软下去。

branches.en: The first sense is the illness in a living body.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是活身体里的病症。

branches.en: The second sense carries the illness into a system.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把病带进一个制度。

branches.en: Both senses describe something that spreads by itself.
branches.cn: 两个义项都形容会自己蔓延的东西。

branches.en: Both need a name before they can be fought.
branches.cn: 两个义项都要先有名字才好对付。

branches.en: Only the second sense is used about money or power.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项会用在金钱或权力上。

intro.en: Disease belongs to the ease family, where comfort, difficulty and illness share one stem.
intro.cn: disease 属于 ease 一族，安适、容易与疾病共用同一词干。

latinIntro.en: Old French aise, comfort, joins des- to make desaise, and English keeps several relatives of the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 古法语 aise（安适）加 des- 成为 desaise，英语保留了同一词干的几个亲属。

items.example: He felt uneasy at the door.
A small unease stayed with her.
The diseased tree was cut down.

definition_zh: 功能；作用；函数；运转
definition_en: the purpose or role of something, a mathematical relation, or to work properly
core_image: 一台旧机器的齿轮重新咬合并平稳转动
scene: 这台旧机器仍然运转良好。 The old machine still functions well.
sceneCN: 这里 function 是「运转」（第 3 个义项）；句意：这台旧机器仍然运转良好。

derivatives.zh: 功能的；实用的
功能上；实用地
故障

senses.title: The purpose of a thing
senses.definition: the purpose or use of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物的用途或作用
senses.example: The main function of a knife is cutting.
senses.exampleCN: 刀的主要功能是切割。
senses.why: This is the general role sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是通用的作用义项。

senses.title: A mathematical relation
senses.definition: a mathematical relation between two sets of values
senses.definitionCN: 两组数值之间的数学关系
senses.example: The graph shows a simple function.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅图显示一个简单的函数。
senses.why: Mathematics uses the word for a precise relation.
senses.whyCN: 数学用这个词表示精确关系。

senses.title: Work properly
senses.definition: to work or operate correctly
senses.definitionCN: 正确工作或运转
senses.example: The old machine still functions well.
senses.exampleCN: 这台旧机器仍然运转良好。
senses.why: The noun became a verb of working.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为表示工作的动词。

intro.en: Function comes from Latin functio, meaning performance.
intro.cn: function 来自拉丁语 functio，意为执行、履行。

items.en: Functio meant performance or discharge of duty.
items.cn: functio 意为执行或履行职责。

items.en: Fungi meant to perform or carry out.
items.cn: fungi 意为执行或完成。

items.en: The word entered English as function.
items.cn: 这个词以 function 进入英语。

items.en: Mathematics gave it the sense of a relation.
items.cn: 数学赋予它「关系」的义项。

items.en: The verb came to mean to operate.
items.cn: 动词义发展为「运转」。

note.en: Function is compared with look-alike words and words for purpose.
note.cn: 把 function 与形近词以及表示用途的词作比较。

entries.definition: a place where roads meet
a part of a whole number
stories that are not true
the part someone or something plays
the reason for doing something
to work or control a machine

normalIntro.en: A function is what something is for, or whether it works.
normalIntro.cn: function 是某物的用途，或它是否运转。

normal.en: The old machine still functions well.
normal.cn: 这台旧机器仍然运转良好。

normal.en: The main function of a knife is cutting.
normal.cn: 刀的主要功能是切割。

normal.en: The graph shows a simple function.
normal.cn: 这幅图显示一个简单的函数。

normal.en: The heart's function is to pump blood.
normal.cn: 心脏的功能是泵血。

normal.en: This room can function as an office.
normal.cn: 这个房间可以充当办公室。

abstract.en: Every part has a function, even if no one sees it.
abstract.cn: 每个部件都有作用，即使没人看见。

abstract.en: A thing can keep its shape and lose its function.
abstract.cn: 事物可以保持外形却失去功能。

abstract.en: Purpose is the quiet engine of daily work.
abstract.cn: 目的是日常工作的安静发动机。

examples.en: The old machine still functions well.
examples.cn: 这台旧机器仍然运转良好。

examples.en: The main function of a knife is cutting.
examples.cn: 刀的主要功能是切割。

examples.en: This room can function as an office.
examples.cn: 这个房间可以充当办公室。

dict_mnemonic.text: function 与 junction、fraction 形近；functional 是「实用的」，malfunction 是「故障」。

root: 源自拉丁语 functio（执行、履行），词根 fungi 意为「完成」；核心义「发挥作用」。

sensesIntro.en: Function means a purpose, a mathematical relation, or to operate correctly.
sensesIntro.cn: function 意为功能、数学函数，或正确运转。

core.en: The work something is made to do.
core.cn: 某物被造出来要做的工作。

branches.en: A tool does its intended job.
branches.cn: 工具完成它被设计的工作。

branches.en: Numbers connect by a fixed rule.
branches.cn: 数字按固定规则相连。

branches.en: A machine keeps running.
branches.cn: 机器持续运转。

branches.en: Purpose and working are two sides of one idea.
branches.cn: 用途与运转是同一观念的两面。

branches.en: Even abstract rules describe how things work.
branches.cn: 即使抽象规则也描述事物如何运作。

intro.en: Function forms words for roles and working parts.
intro.cn: function 构成表示作用和运作部件的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base funct- means performing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 funct- 意为执行。

items.example: The function of a key is to open.
The old pump functioned for years.
The kitchen is small but functional.
The box functions as a table.
The main function is to store data.

definition_zh: 精神的；心灵的；宗教的；与灵魂有关的；（名）黑人灵歌
definition_en: connected with the human spirit or soul rather than the body or material things
core_image: 身体之外的那部分人：摸不着，却撑着人站直
scene: 山间小教堂的木窗透进晨光。 The choir sang a spiritual about crossing the river home.
sceneCN: 这里 spiritual 是「灵歌」（第 5 个义项：宗教歌曲，多指黑人灵歌）；句意为唱诗班演唱了一首关于渡河归家的灵歌。图中可辨识物件：小教堂、木窗、唱诗班。

pos.zh: 形容词：精神的；心灵的；宗教的
名词：灵歌（多指黑人灵歌）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「在精神上」
本词的名词基础，义为「精神；灵魂」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「灵性；精神性」
由同族名词加后缀构成，义为「精神饱满的」

senses.title: Of the spirit rather than the body
senses.definition: relating to the spirit or soul rather than to the body or physical things
senses.definitionCN: 与精神或灵魂相关，而非身体或物质
senses.example: Music met her spiritual needs after the illness.
senses.exampleCN: 病后音乐满足了她的精神需求。
senses.why: The hand cannot grasp this part of a person: it stands where matter ends.
senses.whyCN: 手抓不住人的这一部分：它站在物质尽头之处。

senses.title: Of religion or sacred things
senses.definition: connected with religion or the sacred
senses.definitionCN: 与宗教或神圣之事相关
senses.example: The temple is the spiritual centre of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 这座寺庙是山谷的宗教中心。
senses.why: The breath within becomes breath before the divine.
senses.whyCN: 体内之气化为面对神圣的呼吸。

senses.title: Of inner growth and depth
senses.definition: concerned with inner development, meaning, or depth of life
senses.definitionCN: 关乎内在发展、生命意义或深度
senses.example: His journals record a slow spiritual awakening.
senses.exampleCN: 他的日记记录了一场缓慢的心灵觉醒。
senses.why: The hidden person grows like roots below the visible stem.
senses.whyCN: 隐藏之人如可见茎干下的根系在生长。

senses.title: Not material or worldly
senses.definition: not made of matter or tied to worldly concerns
senses.definitionCN: 不由物质构成，不系于世俗关切
senses.example: The letter speaks of wealth that is spiritual, not gold.
senses.exampleCN: 信中所言财富是精神的，而非黄金。
senses.why: What has no weight may still be the heaviest thing a person owns.
senses.whyCN: 没有重量的东西可能是一个人所拥有的最重之物。

senses.title: A religious song, especially a Black spiritual
senses.definition: a religious folk song, especially one created by enslaved African Americans
senses.definitionCN: 宗教民歌，尤指被奴役的非裔美国人创作的歌曲
senses.example: The choir performed old spirituals at the festival.
senses.exampleCN: 唱诗班在音乐节上演唱了古老的灵歌。
senses.why: The adjective freezes into a noun: the sacred breath takes the form of song.
senses.whyCN: 形容词凝为名词：神圣的呼吸化为歌的形式。

senses.title: Clerical or church-related
senses.definition: belonging to the church or its ministry rather than civil affairs
senses.definitionCN: 属于教会及其神职而非世俗事务
senses.example: The court gave the church spiritual jurisdiction over marriage.
senses.exampleCN: 法院给予教会对婚姻的宗教管辖权。
senses.why: The inner realm gets its own government, beside the state.
senses.whyCN: 内在领域在国家之外另立治理。

senses.title: Living, quickening, as breath
senses.definition: giving life or liveliness, in older or literary usage
senses.definitionCN: 赋予生命或生气，见于旧用法或文学用法
senses.example: The poet calls sleep the spiritual restoration of the weary.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人称睡眠为疲惫者灵性的复原。
senses.why: Breath was the sign of life, so whatever quickens a thing is spiritual.
senses.whyCN: 气息是生命的标记，故凡赋予生气者皆为 spiritual。

senses.title: Immaterial beings and their realm
senses.definition: belonging to immaterial beings or their world
senses.definitionCN: 属于非物质存在或其世界
senses.example: Old stories fill the hills with spiritual presences.
senses.exampleCN: 古老故事里满是山间的灵性存在。
senses.why: The breath that outlives the body gathers into an unseen realm.
senses.whyCN: 比身体长存之气聚成一个看不见的领域。

intro.en: Spiritual is the adjective of the Latin breath-word, carried into English through church Latin.
intro.cn: spiritual 是拉丁「气息」词的形容词形式，经教会拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: (s)peis- is generally reconstructed as "to blow, breathe"; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 (s)peis- 表示「吹、呼吸」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Latin spiritus meant "breath", later "soul, courage".
items.cn: 拉丁语 spiritus 意为「气息」，后指「灵魂、勇气」。

items.en: Late Latin spiritualis meant "of the spirit, of the breath", used heavily by church writers.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 spiritualis 意为「属于灵的、属于气息的」，教会作家大量使用。

items.en: The word moved through Old French spirituel and ecclesiastical Latin into English.
items.cn: 该词经古法语 spirituel 与教会拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: English spiritual first marked the religious sphere, later inner life and the song tradition.
items.cn: 英语 spiritual 最早标示宗教领域，后指内在生活与灵歌传统。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the breathing family and near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers words of the inner and sacred life.
note.cn: 形近组收「呼吸」词族与拼写相近的词；近义组收表示内在与神圣生活的词。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being concerned with the spirit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指关注精神的性质。

entries.definition: Full of energy; shares the same noun base spirit.
entries.definitionCN: 精力充沛；与 spiritual 共享名词基础 spirit。

entries.definition: To encourage; built on the same breath-word.
entries.definitionCN: 鼓舞；建立在同一「气息」词上。

entries.definition: An adjective of strong liquor; same family, different branch.

normal.en: A spiritual in music is a sacred folk song.
normal.cn: 音乐中的 spiritual 是神圣的民歌。

normal.en: The same family gives spirituality and spirituous.

normal.en: Spiritual jurisdiction once meant the church court's realm.

abstract.cn: 想象一个人立于两界：脚在土上，头在流动的气中。

abstract.en: The part of you that cannot be photographed is the spiritual part.
abstract.cn: 无法被拍摄的那部分你，就是 spiritual 部分。

abstract.en: A song that carries the breath of a suffering people is called a spiritual.
abstract.cn: 承载受难民族气息的歌，被称为灵歌。

examples.en: Reading was for him a form of spiritual exercise.
examples.cn: 对他而言，阅读是一种心灵锻炼。

examples.en: The spirituals preserved stories of hope and escape.
examples.cn: 这些灵歌保存了希望与出逃的故事。

examples.en: The town built a hospital for physical and spiritual care.
examples.cn: 小镇建起一座兼顾身体与心灵照护的医院。

root: spiritual 由 spirit 加形容词后缀 -ual 构成；spirit 来自拉丁语 spiritus「气息」，由 spirare「呼吸」派生，一般认为源于原始印欧语 (s)peis-「吹、呼吸」，更早来源不确定；晚期拉丁语 spiritualis 为教会用语，经古法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of spiritual climb from the breath upward: the inner person, the sacred, the immaterial, and the song that carries it all.
sensesIntro.cn: spiritual 的各项义项从气息向上攀：内在之人、神圣、非物质，以及承载这一切的歌。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person with feet on soil and head breathing in moving air.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人脚踩泥土，头在流动的气中呼吸。

branches.en: THE INNER LINE: needs and growth that no market can weigh.
branches.cn: 内在线：市场无法称量的需求与成长。

branches.en: THE SACRED LINE: the divine realm and the church jurisdiction that guards it.
branches.cn: 神圣线：神圣领域及守护它的教会管辖权。

branches.en: THE IMMATERIAL LINE: weightless wealth and unseen presences in the hills.
branches.cn: 非物质线：无重量的财富与山间无形的存在。

branches.en: THE QUICKENING LINE: whatever gives life is breath, and breath is spirit.
branches.cn: 赋生线：凡赋予生命者皆气息，气息即灵。

branches.en: THE SONG LINE: the adjective freezes into the noun for sacred folk song.
branches.cn: 歌线：形容词凝为名词，指神圣的民歌。

intro.en: Spiritual stacks the Latin breath-word with an adjective suffix, and English keeps branching it.
intro.cn: spiritual 把拉丁「气息」词与形容词后缀叠合；英语继续在其上分支。

latinIntro.en: Latin spiritus, spirare and Late Latin spiritualis are recorded; the Indo-European root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spiritus、spirare 与晚期拉丁语 spiritualis 均有记录，印欧词根为重构形式。

senses.title: One thing in a set
senses.definition: a single object among a number of similar things, especially in a shop or a set
senses.definitionCN: 一批同类东西中的单独一件，常用于商店或成套物品
senses.example: Every item in the box was checked twice.
senses.exampleCN: 箱子里的每件物品都查了两遍。
senses.why: The word began as a single entry in a list, and a thing in a shop is one such entry.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指清单上的单独一条，商店里的那件东西正是这样一条。

senses.title: A point on a list
senses.definition: one point or entry in a list, agenda, or order of business
senses.definitionCN: 清单、议程或议事程序中的一条
senses.example: The first item on the agenda is the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 议程上的第一项是预算。
senses.why: The list sense is the oldest one, and each numbered line is still an item.
senses.whyCN: 清单义最古老，每一条编号的行仍然叫 item。

senses.title: A clause in a document
senses.definition: one separate article or clause in a contract, law, or set of rules
senses.definitionCN: 合同、法律或规章中单独的一条
senses.example: Item three of the contract sets the payment date.
senses.exampleCN: 合同第三条规定了付款日期。
senses.why: A legal clause is a list entry written by lawyers, so the same word fits.
senses.whyCN: 法律条款是律师写下的清单条目，于是同一个词也适用。

senses.title: One piece of news
senses.definition: a short single report in a newspaper, broadcast, or news feed
senses.definitionCN: 报纸、广播或信息流中单独的一条报道
senses.example: A short news item mentioned the bridge closure.
senses.exampleCN: 一条短新闻提到了那座桥封闭的消息。
senses.why: A news page is a list of reports, and each report is one item on it.
senses.whyCN: 新闻版面就是一串报道，每篇都是上面的一条。

senses.title: Two people as a couple
senses.definition: used in old-fashioned or humorous speech for two people known to be a couple
senses.definitionCN: 旧式或玩笑说法，指大家知道的一对情侣
senses.example: They are an item again after the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天过后他们又成了一对。
senses.why: A couple becomes a single entry in gossip, so two people are listed as one thing.
senses.whyCN: 一对情侣在闲谈里变成一个条目，于是两个人被当成一样东西列出来。

intro.en: Item is the Latin word item, meaning "likewise, in the same way", used to begin each separate entry in a list.
intro.cn: item 就是拉丁语 item「同样地」，原本用在清单每一条的开头，后来被当成那一条本身。

items.en: item was an adverb meaning likewise or also.
items.cn: item 是副词，意为同样地、也。

items.en: In lists and accounts each line began with item, so the word marked one entry.
items.cn: 在清单和账簿里每一行都以 item 开头，于是这个词标记一条记录。

items.en: Old French took item as a noun for an entry in a list.
items.cn: 古法语把 item 用作名词，指清单里的一条。

items.en: English borrowed it for a statement in an account or inventory.
items.cn: 英语借来指账目或清册中的一项。

items.en: The meaning widened from list entry to any single thing.
items.cn: 词义从清单条目扩展到任何单独的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ite-/item- shape; the near-meaning group holds words for single things and list entries.
note.cn: 形近组共用 ite-、item- 形状；近义组收表示单件物品与清单条目的词。

core_image: 孩子张开双臂扑向的那个人：最亲的怀抱
scene: 小女孩摔破了膝盖，哭着满屋子找人。" Mommy, I need a bandage!" she called from the hallway.
sceneCN: 这里 mommy 是「妈妈、妈咪」（第 1 个义项：孩子对母亲的亲昵称呼）；句意是小女孩在走廊里喊「妈妈，我需要创可贴」。

senses.title: A child's affectionate word for mother
senses.definition: the word a small child uses to call or talk about its mother, showing closeness and affection
senses.definitionCN: 小孩子呼唤或提及母亲时用的词，表示亲近与依恋
senses.example: The toddler reached out her arms and whispered, "Mommy."
senses.exampleCN: 刚学步的小女孩张开双臂，轻声喊「妈妈」。
senses.why: Baby talk favors the easiest syllables ma-ma, so the affectionate reduplicated form became the child's name for the person who holds and feeds them.
senses.whyCN: 儿语偏爱最容易发的叠音 ma-ma，这个重复的亲昵形式自然成为孩子对那个怀抱自己、喂养自己的人的称呼。

senses.title: A mother figure viewed through a child's eyes
senses.definition: a mother regarded from the child's perspective, as the one who comforts, protects and decides
senses.definitionCN: 从孩子视角看的母亲——那个安慰、保护并替自己做决定的人
senses.example: Only mommy can kiss the pain away and make the tears stop.
senses.exampleCN: 只有妈妈能吻走疼痛，让眼泪停下来。
senses.why: Because the word belongs to the child's world, it carries the child's view of the mother: comfort-giver, protector and authority in one small person.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词属于孩子的世界，它天然带着孩子眼中的母亲形象：安慰者、保护者，以及孩子小世界里说了算的人。

intro.en: Mommy belongs to the universal family of nursery syllables built on ma-, the sound babies make earliest and most easily.
intro.cn: mommy 属于以 ma- 为基础的儿语大家族——这是婴儿最早、最容易发出的音。

items.en: The reconstructed nursery form *mma / *ama, a reduplicated labial syllable, is generally believed to be the origin of mother words across many unrelated languages.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构形式 *mma / *ama 是一个重复的唇音音节，是许多互不相关语言中「母亲」一词的共同源头。

items.en: Old English had modor for the adult word, while nursery forms such as mamme were used by children in speech.
items.cn: 古英语的正式称呼是 modor，儿语中则使用 mamme 一类的形式。

items.en: Forms like mame and mamme appear in child-directed speech; mamma and momme variants spread through the nursery vocabulary.
items.cn: mame、mamme 等形式出现在面向幼儿的话语中，mamma、momme 等变体在儿语词汇中流传。

items.en: Mamma became fashionable in polite speech; in America the shortened mom arose, with mommy as its diminutive.
items.cn: mamma 在文雅口语中风行；美国产生了缩短形式 mom，mommy 则是其亲昵小称。

items.en: Mommy established itself as the standard American nursery word for mother, alongside British mummy.
items.cn: mommy 成为美式英语中称呼母亲的标准儿语词，与英式的 mummy 并行。

items.en: Today mommy is the affectionate child's word for mother in American English, also used playfully by adults.
items.cn: 如今 mommy 是美式英语中孩子对母亲的亲昵称呼，成人有时也戏谑使用。

note.en: Do not confuse the nursery word mommy with its formal cousin mother, or with the British spelling mummy, which also names an Egyptian wrapped corpse.
note.cn: 不要把儿语 mommy 与正式的 mother 混淆，也不要与英式拼写 mummy 混淆——后者还指埃及木乃伊。

entries.definition: the British nursery word for mother, identical in origin but spelled differently; also a preserved dead body in ancient Egypt
entries.definitionCN: 英式儿语「妈妈」，与 mommy 同源但拼写不同；另指古埃及木乃伊（同一拼写，另一词源）

entries.definition: an older nursery form for mother, also the anatomical term mamma for a breast or milk gland
entries.definitionCN: 更古老的儿语「妈妈」形式；解剖学中 mamma 又指乳房、乳腺

entries.definition: the everyday American short form of mother, less childish than mommy and usable by adults
entries.definitionCN: 美式英语中 mother 的日常简称，比 mommy 少一些孩子气，成人也常用

entries.definition: the standard word for a female parent, neutral in register where mommy is baby talk
entries.definitionCN: 「母亲」的标准说法，语体中性；mommy 则是儿语

entries.definition: an informal, slightly old-fashioned word for mother, built on the same baby sound ma-
entries.definitionCN: 「妈妈」的非正式说法，略带旧时口吻，同样建立在婴儿音 ma- 上

entries.definition: a clipped colloquial word for mother, common in informal American speech
entries.definitionCN: 「妈」的口语缩略说法，美式非正式口语常用

normalIntro.en: Use the baby sound and the family spellings to fix mommy in memory.
normalIntro.cn: 用婴儿音和同族拼写把 mommy 牢牢记住。

normal.en: mommy = mom + -y; the suffix -y makes any word sound small and affectionate, so mom + y = "dear mom".
normal.cn: mommy = mom + -y；后缀 -y 让词带上「小而亲昵」的口吻，mom 加 y 就是「亲爱的妈妈」。

normal.en: The first syllable ma- is the oldest baby sound in the world: mama → mom → mommy all grow from it.
normal.cn: 首音节 ma- 是世界上最古老的婴儿音：mama → mom → mommy 都由它生长而来。

normal.en: Compare the spelling pair: American mommy versus British mummy — remember "America has an o, Britain has a u".
normal.cn: 对比拼写：美式 mommy 与英式 mummy——记住「美国用 o，英国用 u」。

normal.en: mommy and daddy rhyme in feeling: both end in -y and both are the child's first names for parents.
normal.cn: mommy 与 daddy 韵味相配：都以 -y 结尾，都是孩子对父母最初的称呼。

normal.en: The plural follows the -y → -ies rule like baby → babies: mommy → mommies.
normal.cn: 复数遵循 -y 变 -ies 的规则，与 baby → babies 相同：mommy → mommies。

abstract.en: Picture a toddler tugging a skirt and repeating ma-ma-ma until the word mommy is born.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小孩拽着裙角反复喊 ma-ma-ma，直到 mommy 这个词诞生。

abstract.en: Hear the -y at the end as a warm little smile attached to the word mom.
abstract.cn: 把词尾的 -y 听成贴在 mom 后面的一个温暖的小微笑。

abstract.en: Feel the chain of closeness: mother (formal) → mom (everyday) → mommy (a child's hug in word form).
abstract.cn: 感受亲昵的链条：mother（正式）→ mom（日常）→ mommy（一个孩子式的拥抱变成了词）。

examples.en: "Mommy, will you read me a story?" asked the little boy at bedtime.
examples.cn: 「妈妈，你能给我读个故事吗？」小男孩睡前问。

examples.en: The worried mommy waited outside the classroom on the first day of school.
examples.cn: 开学第一天，忧心的妈妈在教室外等候。

examples.en: Every mother was once somebody's little child calling for mommy.
examples.cn: 每位母亲都曾是某个喊着要妈妈的小小孩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「毛米」——小孩子口齿不清，把「妈咪」喊成「毛米」，毛茸茸的怀抱里是妈妈；mommy 由此记牢。

root: 一般认为源自婴儿最早的唇音叠音节 ma-ma（重构形式 *mma / *ama），属于跨语言的儿语普遍现象；mommy 是 mom 加亲昵后缀 -y 的形式，与古英语 mamme、中世纪英语 mamme 同族，并非拉丁词根，故无拉丁同源词。

sensesIntro.en: From the baby sound ma-ma, mommy first names the mother a child calls for, then extends to the mother figure as the child sees her.
sensesIntro.cn: 从婴儿音 ma-ma 出发，mommy 先指孩子呼唤的母亲，再引申为孩子眼中的母亲角色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child's arms reaching for the one person who is comfort and safety
core.cn: 核心意象：孩子张开双臂扑向的那个既是安慰又是安全的人

branches.en: The nursery sound becomes the child's word for mother
branches.cn: 儿语音成为孩子对母亲的称呼

branches.en: Calling the name is calling for comfort and help
branches.cn: 喊出称呼就是在呼唤安慰与帮助

branches.en: The mother figure stands as protector in the child's small world
branches.cn: 母亲角色在孩子的小世界里充当保护者

branches.en: Authority and decisions also belong to this figure
branches.cn: 这一角色也是孩子世界里做主的人

branches.en: The -y ending wraps the whole bond in affection
branches.cn: 后缀 -y 给整层亲情裹上亲昵的外衣

intro.en: Mommy is not built from Latin roots; its parts are the baby syllable ma- and the English affectionate suffix -y.
intro.cn: mommy 并非由拉丁词根构成；它的组成是婴儿音节 ma- 和英语亲昵后缀 -y。

latinIntro.en: Latin has no cognate here: the word belongs to nursery language, so the Latin-related slot stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语在此无同源词：这个词属于儿语范畴，拉丁相关条目留空。

items.meaning: the earliest baby sound, base of mother words worldwide
items.meaningCN: 最早的婴儿音，全世界「母亲」一词的基础
items.example: mama is almost the same in hundreds of unrelated languages
items.exampleCN: mama 在数百种互不相关的语言中几乎一模一样

items.meaning: makes a word small, familiar, affectionate
items.meaningCN: 使词带上「小、熟稔、亲昵」的口吻
items.exampleCN: dog 变 doggy，mom 加 y 变 mommy

items.meaning: another affectionate ending in family words
items.meaningCN: 家庭称呼里另一个亲昵词尾
items.exampleCN: aunt 变 auntie，再加 granny 一词

items.example: mommyhood describes life as a mommy
items.exampleCN: mommyhood 描述为人母的生活

items.meaning: the formal base word for a female parent
regional short forms of mother (British mum, American mom)
items.meaningCN: mother 的地域简称（英式 mum、美式 mom）
items.example: mum is the British everyday word

items.meaning: British spelling of mommy; separately, an embalmed body
items.meaningCN: mommy 的英式拼写；另有「木乃伊」义（不同词源）
items.example: British children say mummy, American children say mommy
items.exampleCN: 英国孩子说 mummy，美国孩子说 mommy

items.meaning: a career path slowed down for child care
items.meaningCN: 为照顾孩子而放缓的职业路径
items.example: she chose the mommy track for two years
items.exampleCN: 她选择了两年的妈妈轨道

derivatives.zh: mommy 加 -hood 构成，义为「妈妈身份；为人母的状态」
mommy 的口语缩短形式，义为「妈妈」
同族儿语形式，义为「妈妈」

definition_zh: 极其重要的、必不可少的；维持生命所必需的；有活力的、生机勃勃的
definition_en: extremely important and necessary; connected with or needed for life; full of energy
core_image: 跳动的脉搏：少了它生命就停下来的那一件事
scene: 手术室的仪器发出规律的滴声，监护屏上的波线从未中断。 Clean water is vital for the patients' recovery.
sceneCN: 这里 vital 是「必不可少的」（第 2 个义项：对生命或结果不可或缺）；句意为清洁用水对病人的康复至关重要。像脉搏一样不能停，就是这个词。

pos.zh: 形容词：极其重要的；维持生命所必需的；有活力的

collocations.zh: 一座生机勃勃、不断发展的城市

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「活力、生命力」，由 vital 加 -ity 构成
副词，义为「极其、紧要地」
动词，义为「使充满活力」，较少使用
动词，义为「使恢复生机」，由 re- 加 vitalize 构成
名词，义为「维生素」，与 vital 同源词族

senses.title: Necessary for life
senses.definition: needed by a living body to stay alive
senses.definitionCN: 生物体存活所必需的
senses.example: The monitors tracked each patient's vital signs.
senses.exampleCN: 监护仪追踪每位病人的生命体征。
senses.why: Latin vita means life; anything tied to life itself is vital.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vita 意为生命；与生命本身相连的即是 vital。

senses.title: Extremely important
senses.definition: so important that something fails without it
senses.definitionCN: 重要到缺少它事情就无法进行的
senses.example: Clean water is vital for the patients' recovery.
senses.exampleCN: 清洁用水对病人的康复至关重要。
senses.why: What the body cannot live without, a plan cannot succeed without: life's logic applied to work.
senses.whyCN: 身体离之不能活的东西，计划离之不能成：生命的逻辑用到事务上。

senses.title: Full of energy
senses.definition: lively, energetic, and full of strength
senses.definitionCN: 有生气、精力充沛、充满力量的
senses.example: She remained vital well into her nineties.
senses.exampleCN: 她年逾九十仍然活力不减。
senses.why: Where life concentrates, energy shows; the word brightens with living force.
senses.whyCN: 生命力聚集之处便显出能量，这个词随之带上生气的光亮。

senses.title: Deathly or life-related in old use
senses.definition: relating to life and death, in older or formal use
senses.definitionCN: 涉及生死，见于旧式或正式用法
senses.example: The wound struck a vital part.
senses.exampleCN: 伤口击中了要害部位。
senses.why: The parts that hold life are the parts whose loss ends it.
senses.whyCN: 维系生命的部位，一旦失去便终结生命，故称要害。

intro.en: Vital is Latin vita, life, turned into an adjective: everything that belongs to life.
intro.cn: vital 由拉丁语 vita（生命）变成的形容词：一切属于生命的东西。

items.en: The reconstructed root *gweih- means to live, behind both Latin vivere and vita.
items.cn: 重构词根 *gweih- 意为活，是拉丁 vivere 与 vita 的共同来源。

items.en: Vita means life; vitalis means of life, life-giving, or necessary to life.
items.cn: 拉丁语 vita 意为生命；vitalis 意为属于生命的、给予生命的。

items.en: The word passes through French vital with the same senses.
items.cn: 该词经法语 vital 传入，义项基本不变。

items.en: English takes vital in medical and theological texts, meaning of life or essential to it.
items.cn: 英语在医学与神学文本中先取 vital，意为生命的或生命必需的。

items.en: The everyday sense of extremely important grows from the medical one, and the energetic sense keeps the Latin fire.
items.cn: 「极其重要」的日常义由医学义生长而来，而「有活力」义保留了拉丁语的生命之火。

note.en: Look-alikes share the life-root or the spelling; near meanings range from essential to lively.
note.cn: 形近组共享「生命」词根或拼写，近义组从「不可或缺」延伸到「活泼」。

entries.definition: energy and liveliness
entries.definitionCN: 活力、生命力；vital 加 -ity 构成

entries.definition: a substance needed for health, coined as the amine of life
entries.definitionCN: 维生素；造词时取「生命之胺」之意，同 vita 词根

entries.definition: the organs necessary for life
entries.definitionCN: 生命器官（心、肺等）；vital 的复数名词用法

entries.definition: a small bottle for medicine
entries.definitionCN: 小药瓶；与 vital 拼写相近但词源为拉丁 phialis（玻璃瓶），不同源

entries.definition: food or provisions, old use
entries.definitionCN: 食物、给养（旧用法）；发音与 vital 相近，词根为拉丁 victualia（给养），词源不同

entries.definition: absolutely necessary
entries.definitionCN: 必需的；与极其重要义相邻，essential 强调本质，vital 强调性命攸关

entries.definition: deciding success or failure
entries.definitionCN: 决定成败的；强调关键节点

entries.definition: impossible to do without
entries.definitionCN: 不可或缺的；语气更绝对

entries.definition: of decisive importance or at a turning point
entries.definitionCN: 关键的、危急的；兼有临界义

entries.definition: full of energy
entries.definitionCN: 精力充沛的；与有活力义相邻，不含生命必需义

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from Latin vita, life.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，全部来自拉丁语 vita（生命）。

normal.en: vita means life; vital means belonging to life.
normal.cn: vita 意为生命；vital 即属于生命的。

normal.en: vital signs are the readings that show a body is alive.
normal.cn: vital signs 是显示身体存活的生命体征。

normal.en: vitamin was coined as the amine of life.
normal.cn: vitamin 造词时意为「生命之胺」。

normal.en: revitalize is to give life back, re- plus vitalize.
normal.cn: revitalize 是重新赋予生机，re- 加 vitalize。

normal.en: a vital organ is one the body cannot lose and live.
normal.cn: vital organ 是身体失去即无法存活的器官。

abstract.en: A pulse on a screen: the line that must never go flat.
abstract.cn: 屏幕上的脉搏：那条绝不能变平的线。

abstract.en: Air in a sealed room: invisible, unnoticed, and suddenly everything.
abstract.cn: 密室中的空气：平时无感，缺时便是一切。

abstract.en: A city at rush hour that still hums after midnight: its vital energy.
abstract.cn: 午夜过后仍然嗡嗡作响的城市：它的活力。

examples.en: Trust is vital to any team that shares one goal.
examples.cn: 信任对任何共赴一目标的团队都至关重要。

examples.en: The nurse checked the patient's vital signs every hour.
examples.cn: 护士每小时检查一次病人的生命体征。

examples.en: Even a small garden can look vital in spring.
examples.cn: 哪怕小花园，春天也能显得生机勃勃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪透」——身体歪透了就没了生命体征；凡是 vital 的东西，歪一点都不行。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源来自拉丁 vita（生命）。

root: 拉丁语 vita（生命）+ 形容词后缀 -alis → vitalis → 法语 vital → 英语 vital。印欧词根 *gweih-（重构形式）同时衍生 vivere（活）、vitamin、revive 等词。

sensesIntro.en: Life first, then everything life depends on, then the brightness of living itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是生命本身，继而是一切生命所依赖之物，最后是生命本身的光亮。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: life itself as the measure of importance
core.cn: 核心意象：以生命本身为重要性的标尺

branches.en: Life in the body: signs, organs, and the parts that hold life
branches.cn: 身体里的生命：体征、器官与维系生命的要害

branches.en: Life's logic borrowed by plans and projects
branches.cn: 计划的逻辑借用生命的逻辑：不可或缺

branches.en: Life showing as energy in a person or city
branches.cn: 生命以能量显现于人或城市

branches.en: What ends things when lost is vital, in body or in plan
branches.cn: 无论身体还是计划，失去即终结者即为 vital

branches.en: From bare survival to flourishing vitality
branches.cn: 从勉强存活到蓬勃生机

intro.en: The life-root spreads through prefixes and suffixes into a family of living words.
intro.cn: 「生命」词根借助前后缀铺成一个「生」义词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin vivere, to live, and vita, life, built the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vivere（活）与 vita（生命）构建了整个词族。

definition_en: in a soft, careful, or mild way
core_image: 双手轻轻托起一只受伤的小鸟
scene: 她轻轻地把婴儿放进摇篮。 She gently laid the baby in the cot.
sceneCN: 这里 gently 是「轻轻地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她轻轻地把婴儿放进摇篮。

derivatives.zh: 温和的；轻柔的
温柔

senses.title: With a light touch
senses.definition: in a soft and careful way that avoids force
senses.definitionCN: 以柔和小心、避免用力的方式
senses.example: She gently laid the baby in the cot.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻轻地把婴儿放进摇篮。
senses.why: The adverb carries the soft touch of gentle into an action.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词把 gentle 的轻柔触感带进了动作。

senses.title: Without force
senses.definition: in a way that is not strong, steep, or sudden
senses.definitionCN: 以不强、不陡、不突然的方式
senses.example: The road rises gently towards the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 道路缓缓向上通向小山。
senses.why: Softness also describes movement and shape.
senses.whyCN: 柔和同样可以形容运动和形状。

senses.title: With care
senses.definition: in a careful way that avoids disturbing someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 以小心的、不打扰人或物的方式
senses.example: He gently woke her with a whisper.
senses.exampleCN: 他用耳语轻轻唤醒她。
senses.why: Gentle action protects what it touches.
senses.whyCN: 温和的动作会保护它所触碰的东西。

intro.en: Gently is the adverb built from gentle and -ly.
intro.cn: gently 是由 gentle 加 -ly 构成的副词。

items.en: Gentil meant noble or well-born.
items.cn: gentil 意为高贵的或出身好的。

items.en: Gentle first described noble character.
items.cn: gentle 最初描述高贵的品格。

items.en: The adverb gently added the -ly ending.
items.cn: 副词 gently 加上了 -ly 后缀。

items.en: It came to describe soft movement and care.
items.cn: 它逐渐形容柔和的动作与小心。

items.en: It is now common with verbs of touch, speech, and motion.
items.cn: 如今它常与触摸、说话和运动的动词连用。

note.en: Gently is compared with look-alike words and adverbs of soft action.
note.cn: 把 gently 与形近词以及表示轻柔动作的副词作比较。

truly and sincerely
in a quiet or gentle way

normalIntro.cn: gently 就是把力度调轻。

normal.en: She gently reminded him of the deadline.
normal.cn: 她委婉地提醒他截止日期。

abstract.en: Move gently and the world moves with you.
abstract.cn: 轻轻行动，世界会与你同行。

abstract.en: A soft word opens a hard door.
abstract.cn: 一句轻柔的话能打开一扇硬门。

abstract.en: Care is strength that knows its own size.
abstract.cn: 小心，是知道自己分量的力量。

examples.en: She gently laid the baby in the cot.

examples.en: He gently woke her with a whisper.
