dict_mnemonic.text: gently 就是 gentle（温和的）加 -ly：gently push 是「轻轻推」，speak gently 是「轻声说」，gently sloping 是「平缓倾斜的」。

root: 由 gentle（温和的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，源自拉丁语 gentilis（同族的、高贵的）。

sensesIntro.en: Gently means with a light touch, without force, or with care.
sensesIntro.cn: gently 意为以轻柔的触碰、不用力的方式，或小心谨慎地。

core.en: Acting with the force turned low.
core.cn: 以调低的力度去行动。

branches.en: A hand lowers a sleeping child.
branches.cn: 一只手把熟睡的孩子放下。

branches.en: A path leans slowly uphill.
branches.cn: 小路缓缓向上倾斜。

branches.en: A whisper wakes someone without alarm.
branches.cn: 一声耳语把人唤醒却不惊扰。

branches.en: Light hands and easy slopes share a small force.
branches.cn: 轻柔的手与缓坡共享很小的力度。

branches.en: Slow motion and careful waking both avoid a shock.
branches.cn: 缓慢的运动与小心的唤醒都避免冲击。

intro.en: Gently is the adverb form of the gentle family.
intro.cn: gently 是 gentle 词族的副词形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source gentilis meant of the same clan.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语来源 gentilis 意为同族的。

items.example: A gentle rain fell all morning.
He treated the bird with gentleness.
A gentler tone calmed the room.
items.exampleCN: 更温和的语气让房间安静下来。

latinEntries.exampleCN: gentilis 是 gently 的源头。

definition_zh: 盎司；少量；一点点；一丝
definition_en: a unit of weight of about twenty-eight grams, with a heavier troy form used for precious metals; also a very small amount or the slightest trace of a quality
core_image: 旧药铺柜台上的一台小铜天平，一端放着待称的小块黄油，另一端是小小的砝码
scene: 旧药铺的柜台上摆着一台小铜天平，药剂师把一小块黄油放上砝码盘，铜指针慢慢停住。 The old recipe asks for one ounce of butter and a pinch of salt.
sceneCN: 这里 ounce 是「盎司」（第 1 个义项：常衡重量单位）；句意为老配方要一盎司黄油加一撮盐，画面是药铺柜台上那台停住的小铜天平。

derivatives.zh: 由 ounce 与 force 复合而成，义为「盎司力」，英制力的单位
由 inch 与 ounce 复合而成，义为「英寸盎司」，英制扭矩单位
由 fluid 与 ounce 复合而成，义为「液量盎司」，用于量液体容积

senses.title: A unit of weight equal to about twenty-eight grams
senses.definition: a unit of weight used in ordinary trade, equal to one sixteenth of a pound or about 28.35 grams
senses.definitionCN: 用于一般贸易的重量单位，等于十六分之一磅，约二十八点三五克
senses.example: Add four ounces of flour to the bowl.
senses.exampleCN: 往碗里加四盎司面粉。
senses.why: Latin uncia named a twelfth part of a larger unit, so the word began as a fraction cut off from something bigger; trade later fixed that fraction into the everyday ounce of sixteen to the pound.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 uncia 本指某一较大单位的十二分之一，所以这个词一开始是「从大单位切下的一份」；后来贸易把这个分数固定成十六分之一磅的日常盎司，分数观念就变成了具体的称重单位。

senses.title: A troy unit used for precious metals
senses.definition: a unit of weight of about 31.1 grams, used for gold, silver and other precious metals
senses.definitionCN: 约三十一点一克的重量单位，用于黄金、白银等贵金属
senses.example: Gold is traded by the troy ounce on world markets.
senses.exampleCN: 黄金在国际市场上按金衡盎司交易。
senses.why: The older twelve-part division survived in the bullion trade after ordinary goods moved to a sixteen-part pound, so one name ended up covering two slightly different weights.
senses.whyCN: 日常货物改用十六分之一磅之后，旧式十二分之一的分法仍在金银交易里活着；同一个名字于是同时指两种略不相同的重量，贵金属这一支保留了更重的古制。

senses.title: A very small quantity
senses.definition: a very small amount of something, often used to stress how little is left or present
senses.definitionCN: 某物极少的一点，常用于强调所剩或所有之少
senses.example: There was not an ounce of sugar left in the jar.
senses.exampleCN: 罐子里一点糖都不剩了。
senses.why: An ounce sits near the bottom of a kitchen scale, so the name of the smallest readable weight drifts easily into a word for a scrap of anything.
senses.whyCN: 盎司落在厨房秤刻度的最低处，于是这个「最小可读重量」的名称很容易滑成「随便一点什么」的说法；义项由称量的下限转向数量上的极小。

senses.title: The slightest trace of a quality
senses.definition: a small but real amount of a feeling or quality, as in an ounce of courage or not an ounce of sense
senses.definitionCN: 某种情感或品质虽少却真实的一点，如「一丝勇气」或「毫无理智」
senses.example: He did not show an ounce of regret for what he had done.
senses.exampleCN: 他对自己做过的事没有表现出一丝悔意。
senses.why: The smallest weight is borrowed to weigh what cannot be put on a scale, so an ounce of a quality means just enough of it to count.
senses.whyCN: 最小的重量被借去称无法放上天平的东西，所以「一丝某种品质」就是刚好够算数的那一点；这次转移靠的是用称重词去量看不见的性情。

intro.en: Ounce descends from a Latin word for a twelfth part, and the same source also gave English inch, which is why a weight and a length share a name.
intro.cn: ounce 上溯自一个表示「十二分之一」的拉丁词，同一来源还给出了英语的 inch，所以一种重量与一种长度共用一段来历。

items.en: Uncia named a twelfth part of a pound or of any larger unit, and it is also the source of the English inch.
items.cn: uncia 指一磅或任何较大单位的十二分之一，也是英语 inch 的来源。

items.en: Old French shortened the Latin word to unce, the form English borrowed for a small weight.
items.cn: 古法语把拉丁词缩为 unce，英语借入时用它指一种小重量。

items.en: Middle English kept the word for a small weight and for a twelfth part, and merchants used it alongside the pound.
items.cn: 中古英语用这个词指小重量，也指十二分之一，商人们把它与磅并用。

items.en: When the sixteen-ounce pound became standard for ordinary goods, the older twelve-part unit stayed in the bullion trade, so one name covered two weights.
items.cn: 当十六盎司为一磅的常衡制成为普通货物的标准，旧的十二进制单位仍留在金银交易中，同一个名字于是覆盖了两种重量。

items.en: Modern English uses ounce for the everyday measure, the troy measure for metals, and figuratively for a very small amount of anything.
items.cn: 现代英语用 ounce 指日常重量、贵金属的金衡重量，也引申指任何东西的极小量。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the Latin twelfth-part word and two words that merely rhyme with ounce; the near-meaning group gathers units of weight and words for a tiny amount.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「十二分之一」一词上的形式，以及两个只是读音相近的词；近义组收重量单位与表示极小量的词。

entries.definition: A unit of length, also descended from Latin uncia, a twelfth part.
entries.definitionCN: 长度单位英寸，同样出自拉丁语 uncia（十二分之一）。

entries.definition: A style of large rounded writing, named from a Latin adjective meaning a twelfth of a foot in height.
entries.definitionCN: 一种大写圆体字，名称出自意为「十二分之一英尺高」的拉丁形容词。

entries.definition: To make something known publicly; the ending looks like ounce but the word comes from Latin nuntius, a messenger.
entries.definitionCN: 公开宣告；词尾看似盎司，实际出自拉丁语 nuntius（信使），只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To spring back after hitting a surface; the spelling echoes ounce but the word is probably imitative and unrelated in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 碰到表面后弹回；拼写与盎司相近，但一般认为出自模仿声音，来源不同。

entries.definition: A metric unit of weight equal to one thousandth of a kilogram.
entries.definitionCN: 公制重量单位，等于千分之一千克。

entries.definition: A unit of weight made of sixteen ounces, or twelve in the troy system.
entries.definitionCN: 由十六盎司组成的重量单位，金衡制中则为十二盎司。

entries.definition: A very small amount of something that is barely there.
entries.definitionCN: 极少、几乎察觉不到的一点。

entries.definition: An extremely small amount, used especially in negative statements.
entries.definitionCN: 极微小的一点，尤用于否定句。

normalIntro.en: The word carries a Latin fraction, a trade weight and a figure of speech, so its hooks return to cutting, weighing and the smallest measurable share.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词带着一个拉丁分数、一个贸易重量和一种说法，记忆钩子都回到切分、称量与最小可称的一份。

normal.en: Uncia meant a twelfth part, so ounce began as a fraction rather than a fixed weight.
normal.cn: uncia 意为十二分之一，所以 ounce 起初是个分数，而不是固定的重量。

normal.en: The same Latin word gave inch, because both were cut from a larger unit by the same habit of dividing into twelve.
normal.cn: 同一拉丁词还给出 inch，因为两者都是按十二等分的老习惯从大单位里切出来的。

normal.en: Troy and avoirdupois are two ways of cutting the pound, and ounce simply followed both.
normal.cn: 金衡与常衡是把磅切成两套办法，ounce 两套都跟着用。

normal.en: Kitchen scales read in ounces, which is why the word can mean a very small amount of anything.
normal.cn: 厨房秤以盎司读数，所以这个词可以指任何东西的极小量。

normal.en: An ounce of courage is the unit turned into a moral measure, weighing a quality on the same scale.
normal.cn: an ounce of courage 是把单位变成品性的量尺，用同一杆秤去称一种性情。

abstract.en: A brass scale on a pharmacy counter, one weight on each pan, is the word at its plainest.
abstract.cn: 药铺柜台上一台铜天平、两盘各放一个砝码，就是这个词最朴素的样子。

abstract.en: A gold bar on a dealer's tray is the same name made heavier by old custom.
abstract.cn: 经销商托盘上的金条，是同一个名字被旧习惯加重后的样子。

abstract.en: A cook adding a single spoonful to a bowl shows a weight unit shrinking into a pinch.
abstract.cn: 厨师往碗里只加一勺，显示一个重量单位缩成了一撮。

examples.en: The recipe asks for one ounce of butter.
examples.cn: 这份配方要求一盎司黄油。

examples.en: Gold is sold by the troy ounce in most markets.
examples.cn: 多数市场上黄金按金衡盎司出售。

examples.en: He did not show an ounce of regret.
examples.cn: 他没有表现出一丝悔意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「盎司」——中文本来就用这两个字音译；称出一小份，正是 ounce。

root: 拉丁语 uncia（十二分之一，也指一种小重量）经古法语 unce 进入英语；同源词还有 inch，因为两者原本都是把一个较大单位切成十二份。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a fraction cut from a larger unit; the senses settle that fraction into a trade weight, split it into troy and ordinary measures, then shrink it into a tiny amount and a trace of character.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是从较大单位切下的一份；义项先把这个分数落成贸易重量，分成金衡与常衡两种量法，再缩小成极小的数量与一丝品性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small brass scale on a pharmacy counter, a lump of butter on one pan, a tiny weight on the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：药铺柜台上的一台小铜天平，一盘放黄油，一盘放小小的砝码。

branches.en: a brass scale on a pharmacy counter
branches.cn: 药铺柜台上的小铜天平

branches.en: a gold bar weighed on a dealer's tray
branches.cn: 经销商托盘上称量的金条

branches.en: a jar scraped almost empty
branches.cn: 几乎刮空的罐子

branches.en: a man refusing to show any regret
branches.cn: 一个人不肯露出半点悔意

branches.en: one small measure, once in grams and once in feeling
branches.cn: 同一种小量，一次按克计，一次按心情计

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin noun for a twelfth part, a French shortening, and a cluster of English compounds that push the same measure into metals, liquids and force.
intro.cn: 这个词依托表示十二分之一的拉丁名词、一个法语缩形，以及一串英语复合词，把同一个量推到金属、液体与力上。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: a unit of length from the same root
items.meaningCN: 同出此词根的长度单位；英寸

items.meaning: the unit used for precious metals
items.meaningCN: 用于贵金属的重量单位

latinEntries.meaning: a twelfth part; a small weight
latinEntries.meaningCN: 十二分之一；小重量单位

definition_zh: 稳定的；平稳的；持续的；（使）稳住；（使）镇定
definition_en: not moving, changing, or shaking; continuing regularly; to make something firm or calm
core_image: 一只手稳稳托住摇晃的水杯——杯中的水面不再颤动
scene: 桥面被风吹得轻轻晃动，工友伸手扶住架子。 He held the ladder steady while his partner climbed up.
sceneCN: 这里 steady 是动词「使稳住」（第 4 个义项：让某物不晃动）；句意为同伴爬梯时他把梯子扶稳了。

pos.zh: 形容词：稳定的；平稳的；持续的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「平稳地；持续地」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「稳定；沉稳」
由否定前缀加本词构成，义为「不稳的；摇晃的」

senses.title: Firmly fixed, not shaking or moving
senses.definition: held or fixed firmly so that it does not shake or wobble
senses.definitionCN: 被牢牢固定、不摇晃不摆动的
senses.example: Keep the camera steady while you take the picture.
senses.exampleCN: 拍照时保持相机稳定。
senses.why: The hand under the cup stops the water surface from trembling.
senses.whyCN: 托住杯子的手让水面不再颤动，即固定不动。

senses.title: Continuing regularly without sudden change
senses.definition: continuing or developing gradually and evenly over time
senses.definitionCN: 随时间平稳均匀地延续或发展
senses.example: The company has shown steady growth for five years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司连续五年稳步增长。
senses.why: The cup that never spills month after month: no sudden tilts.
senses.whyCN: 那只月月不洒的杯子：没有突然的倾斜，即均匀延续。

senses.title: Reliable and calm in character
senses.definition: describing a person who is calm, sensible, and reliable
senses.definitionCN: 形容人冷静、明理、可信赖
senses.example: She is a steady worker who never loses her temper.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个沉稳的员工，从不发脾气。
senses.why: A person who never tilts is trusted the way a firm shelf is trusted.
senses.whyCN: 从不倾斜的人像结实的架子一样被人放心倚靠。

senses.title: To make something firm or stop it shaking
senses.definition: to hold or support something so that it stops moving or shaking
senses.definitionCN: 扶住或支撑某物使其停止晃动
senses.example: He steadied the wobbly table with a folded newspaper.
senses.exampleCN: 他用折起的报纸垫稳了摇晃的桌子。
senses.why: The hand itself goes under the cup: the image turns into an action.
senses.whyCN: 那只手主动伸到杯子下面：意象由状态转为动作。

senses.title: To make someone calm after shock or fear
senses.definition: to help someone become calm again after being frightened or upset
senses.definitionCN: 帮助受惊或心绪不宁的人恢复平静
senses.example: She took a deep breath to steady herself before speaking.
senses.exampleCN: 开口前她深吸一口气让自己镇定下来。
senses.why: Steadying the shaking cup of one's own feelings.
senses.whyCN: 把自己那只情绪之杯扶稳，即让内心不再晃动。

intro.en: Steady comes from stead, the old word for a standing place, plus an adjective ending: fixed in its place.
intro.cn: steady 源自古语 stead（立定之位）加形容词后缀，本义是「固定在其位置上」。

items.en: A reconstructed root *stad- meant to stand or stay fixed.
items.cn: 重构词根 *stad- 意为站立、固定不动。

items.en: Stede meant a place or standing spot, surviving today in stead and instead.
items.cn: 古英语 stede 指地点、立身之处，今存于 stead 与 instead 中。

items.en: Stedfast and stedi described things fixed in their place, firm and unwavering.
items.cn: 中古英语 stedfast、stedi 描述固定在原位、坚定不动之物。

items.en: Steady widened to regular behaviour and dependable character, and became a verb.
items.cn: steady 扩展出「规律、可靠」之义，并发展出动词用法。

items.en: The verb covers both steadying objects and calming people, while go steady named steady courtship.
items.cn: 动词兼指扶稳物件与安抚人心，go steady 则指确定恋爱关系。

note.en: Steady belongs to the stand-place family with stead and instead, and sits near different-root words for firm and calm.
note.cn: steady 与 stead、instead 同属「立定之位」词族，义场又靠近词源不同的「牢固」「镇定」词。

entries.definition: the place or role of someone or something, as in in his stead
entries.definitionCN: 替代之位；与 steady 同根，是本词的名词源头

entries.definition: in the place of something else
entries.definitionCN: 代替；反而；同根复合词，义为「立于其位」

entries.definition: a horse ridden by a knight, a literary word
entries.definitionCN: 坐骑；骏马；拼读相近但词源不同，属文学用语

entries.definition: firmly fixed and not likely to change or fall
entries.definitionCN: 牢固的；稳定的，与 steady 同含「站立」意象且词源相近

entries.definition: solid, strongly fixed, and not moved easily
entries.definitionCN: 坚固的；坚决的，强调不易被动摇

entries.definition: happening all the time or staying the same
entries.definitionCN: 恒定的；不断的，强调持续不变

entries.definition: moving unsteadily from side to side
entries.definitionCN: 摇晃的；不稳的，与 steady 意义相反

normalIntro.en: Use the stead place-root and the real verb patterns to hold each sense firm.
normalIntro.cn: 利用 stead「地点」词根与真实动词搭配把各义项稳稳记住。

normal.en: Steady grows from stead, a standing place, so it means fixed in place.
normal.cn: steady 由 stead（立身之地）生长而来，本义即固定在位。

normal.en: Instead is in stead, in the place of something else, same root.
normal.cn: instead 即 in stead（立于其位），同一词根。

normal.en: Hold steady and steady yourself are the two main verb patterns.
normal.cn: hold steady 与 steady yourself 是两大动词句式，分别指物与人。

normal.en: Go steady is an informal phrase for a steady boyfriend or girlfriend.
normal.cn: go steady 是口语说法，指确定恋人关系。

normal.en: Steadily is the adverb seen in steadily rising prices.
normal.cn: 副词 steadily 常见于 steadily rising prices（价格稳步上涨）。

abstract.en: Picture a hand sliding under a trembling cup until the water surface stills.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手垫到颤动的杯子下面，直到水面静止。

abstract.en: See a growth line on a chart rising evenly, never jumping or dipping.
abstract.cn: 看图表上一条均匀上升的增长线，从不跳升或骤跌。

abstract.en: Feel your own breath slowing to steady yourself before a hard talk.
abstract.cn: 体会艰难谈话前靠呼吸把自己稳住的感受。

examples.en: Prices rose at a steady pace through the summer.
examples.cn: 整个夏天物价平稳上涨。

examples.en: She steadied the bike while the child got on.
examples.cn: 孩子上车时她扶稳了自行车。

examples.en: He is a steady friend who never lets you down.
examples.cn: 他是从不让你失望的可靠朋友。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯代弟」——谐音「四代弟」：家族四代代代相传的买卖，稳稳当当不摇晃。

root: 源自古英语 stede（地点、立定之位，今存于 stead、instead）加形容词后缀 -y，词根一般认为上溯至日耳曼语 *stad-（站立；固定），与 stand 远源相关。

sensesIntro.en: From a thing fixed in its place grow the even passage of time, a reliable character, the act of holding firm, and calming a shaking heart.
sensesIntro.cn: 由「固定在位」生长出时间的均匀延续、可靠的品格、扶稳的动作与安抚人心的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand under a trembling cup until the water stills
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手垫在颤动的杯下，直到水面静止

branches.en: firmly fixed, not wobbling
branches.cn: 固定不摇晃

branches.en: even over time, in work and character
branches.cn: 时间与品格上的均匀、可靠

branches.en: the hand that stops the shaking
branches.cn: 止住晃动的那只手

branches.en: settling one's own trembling feelings
branches.cn: 安抚自己发颤的心绪

branches.en: the still water as both state and result
branches.cn: 静止的水面既是状态也是结果

intro.en: The stead family shows one old place-word branching into fixed, replaced, and mounted ideas.
intro.cn: stead 词族展示了一个古老「地点」词如何派生出固定、替代、坐骑等概念。

latinIntro.en: Steady has no Latin relatives; it is native Germanic, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: steady 没有拉丁同源词，属日耳曼本土词源，故拉丁同族词列表为空。

definition_zh: 否认；拒绝给予
definition_en: to say that something is not true, or to refuse to give something to someone
core_image: 一个人把递到面前的文件推回去，摇了摇头
scene: 记者连问三次，发言人每次都把同一句话重复一遍，眼睛没有离开稿子。 The company denied that it had broken the law.
sceneCN: 这里 deny 指「否认」（第 1 个义项：说某事不是真的）；句意是公司否认自己违反了法律。

derivatives.zh: 否认；拒绝
可否认的
不可否认的
不可否认地
否认者

senses.title: Say it is not true
senses.definition: to state that something is not true
senses.definitionCN: 声明某事不是真的
senses.example: The company denied that it had broken the law.
senses.exampleCN: 公司否认自己违反了法律。
senses.why: A denial pushes a claim back before it can settle.
senses.whyCN: 否认就是把说法在落定之前推回去。

senses.title: Refuse to give
senses.definition: to refuse to allow or give something
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝允许或给予某物
senses.example: He was denied entry to the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 他被拒绝进入大厅。
senses.why: To deny a thing is to shut a door and keep it shut.
senses.whyCN: 拒绝给予，就是关上一扇门并不再打开。

intro.en: Deny came through Old French denier from Latin denegare, where de- means fully and negare means to say no.
intro.cn: deny 经古法语 denier 来自拉丁语 denegare，其中 de- 表示完全，negare 表示说不。

items.en: Denegare joined de-, meaning fully, with negare, to say no.
items.cn: denegare 由 de-（完全）与 negare（说不）合成。

items.en: Writers used denegare for refusing a request or a faith.
items.cn: 作家用 denegare 表示拒绝请求或背弃信仰。

items.en: Denier refused, forbade or said a thing was untrue.
items.cn: denier 可以表示拒绝、禁止，或说某事不实。

items.en: English took deny for both refusing and declaring false.
items.cn: 英语借来 deny，同时表示拒绝与宣布为假。

items.en: Today a person can deny a fact or be denied a chance.
items.cn: 如今人可以否认一个事实，也可能被剥夺一个机会。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the deny stem, and the meaning group moves from refusing a request to rejecting a statement.
note.cn: 形近组共用 deny 词干，近义组则从拒绝请求走到否掉一个说法。

able to be said not to be true

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a document pushed back across a table and end with a door that stays closed.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一份被推回桌对面的文件开始，落到一扇始终关着的门。

normal.en: A shaken head is the shortest denial.
normal.cn: 摇一下头，就是最短的否认。

normal.en: Deny has two hands: one pushes a claim away, one withholds a gift.
normal.cn: deny 有两只手：一只推开说法，一只扣住东西不给。

normal.en: To deny a child a story is to shut a small door.
normal.cn: 不给孩子讲一个故事，就是关上一扇小小的门。

normal.en: A firm denial is a wall built in one sentence.
normal.cn: 一句坚决的否认，就是一句话砌成的一堵墙。

normal.en: Deny and denial differ only in their ending.
normal.cn: deny 与 denial 只差一个词尾。

abstract.en: Picture a palm pressing a sheet of paper flat on a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手掌把一张纸按平在桌上。

abstract.en: Picture a hand closing around a key and putting it away.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手攥住钥匙，把它收了起来。

abstract.en: Picture a doorway with a person standing in it, arms crossed.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在门口，双臂交叉。

examples.en: The company denied that it had broken the law.
examples.cn: 公司否认自己违反了法律。

examples.en: He was denied entry to the hall.
examples.cn: 他被拒绝进入大厅。

examples.en: There is no denying that the plan has failed.
examples.cn: 不可否认，这个计划已经失败。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deny 记成「抵赖」：de 像「抵」，ny 像「赖」，把做过的事抵掉不认，就是否认。

root: 来自拉丁语 denegare，由 de-（完全）与 negare（说不）组成，经古法语 denier 进入英语。它先同时表示拒绝请求与宣布某事不实，后来两条线都保留下来：一条说「这不是真的」，一条说「这个不给你」。

sensesIntro.en: From pushing a claim back across the table to closing the door on a request.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把说法推回桌对面，到对请求关上大门。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet of paper pushed back and a head shaking once.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份文件被推回来，一颗头摇了一下。

branches.en: The first sense is a wall built against a statement.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是针对一个说法砌起的墙。

branches.en: The second sense is a closed hand, not an argument.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是一只攥紧的手，不是一场辩论。

branches.en: Both senses say no, one to a fact and one to a request.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在说不，一个对事实，一个对请求。

branches.en: In argument, deny means the other side has not proved its case.
branches.cn: 在争论里，deny 意味着对方没有证明自己的说法。

branches.en: In daily life, deny means a chance is taken away.
branches.cn: 在日常里，deny 意味着一个机会被拿走了。

intro.en: Deny grows a family of nouns and adjectives about saying no and about what cannot be said no to.
intro.cn: deny 长出一族名词与形容词，讲说不，也讲不容说不。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin negare, to say no, strengthened by de-.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 negare（说不），前面用 de- 加强。

items.meaning: in a way that can be denied
items.exampleCN: 这道命令含糊得可以否认。

definition_zh: 取代；替换；把……放回原处
definition_en: to put something back in its place, or to take the place of something else
core_image: 旧零件被取下，新零件咔哒一声装进同一个位置
scene: 旧电池耗尽后，她把新电池放进遥控器，咔哒一声又能换台了。 She replaced the dead batteries with fresh ones.
sceneCN: 这里 replace 是「替换；更换」（第 3 个义项：用新东西换掉旧东西）；句意：她把没电的电池换成了新电池。

derivatives.zh: 替换；替代者
可替换的
不可替代的

senses.title: To put back in place
senses.definition: to put something back where it was before
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放回它原来所在的位置
senses.example: She replaced the book on the shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 她把书放回书架上。
senses.why: The word is literally re- plus place, so the oldest and most concrete sense is putting something back into its place.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面上就是 re- 加 place，所以最古老、最具体的义项是「放回原位」。

senses.title: To take the place of
senses.definition: to do the job or fill the position of someone or something else
senses.definitionCN: 承担某人或某物的职责，或占据其位置
senses.example: Email has largely replaced the fax.
senses.exampleCN: 电子邮件已在很大程度上取代了传真。
senses.why: If one thing goes back into the same slot, it can push out what was there, which gives the sense of taking over.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个东西回到同一个位置，就可能把原来在那里的东西挤出去，于是产生「接管」之意。

senses.title: To change one thing for another
senses.definition: to remove something and put a new or different thing in its place
senses.definitionCN: 取走某物，并在原位放上新的或不同的事物
senses.example: You should replace the filter every three months.
senses.exampleCN: 你应该每三个月更换一次滤芯。
senses.why: The same slot is filled again, but this time the emphasis falls on the swap between old and new.
senses.whyCN: 同一个位置再次被填满，但这次强调的是新旧之间的对换。

intro.en: Replace is an English formation from re- and place, where place comes through French from Latin platea, a broad street.
intro.cn: replace 是英语用 re- 与 place 构成的词，而 place 经由法语来自拉丁语 platea（宽阔的街道）。

items.en: Platea means a broad street or open square, and later a position or site.
items.cn: platea 指宽阔的街道或开阔的广场，后来也指位置或场地。

items.en: Old French place narrows the word to a position, spot, or room.
items.cn: 古法语 place 把词义收窄为位置、地点或空间。

items.en: Middle English place names a location as well as a rank or role.
items.cn: 中古英语 place 既指地点，也指位次或角色。

items.en: English speakers add re- to place to make replace, meaning put back.
items.cn: 英语使用者给 place 加 re- 构成 replace，意为「放回」。

items.en: The sense widens from putting back to filling a position left by another.
items.cn: 词义从「放回」扩展到「填补他人留下的位置」。

items.en: Modern English uses replace for both restoring and substituting.
items.cn: 现代英语中 replace 既可表示放回，也可表示替换。

note.en: Replace sits between putting back and swapping out, and its family covers the act, the ability, and the impossibility of substitution.
note.cn: replace 介于「放回」与「换掉」之间，其词族涵盖替换的动作、可能性与不可替代性。

entries.definition: the act of replacing, or the thing that replaces
able to be replaced
too special to be replaced
to use one thing instead of another
to replace something, especially by force or over time
entries.definitionCN: 取代，尤指逐步或强行取代

entries.definition: to force something out of its usual place
to put something back into its former state

normalIntro.en: Replace is transparent: re- means again, and place means position, so the word pictures something returning to a slot.
normalIntro.cn: replace 的构词很透明：re- 表示再次，place 表示位置，合起来就是「重新回到一个位置」。

normal.en: Re- plus place: put it back in place.
normal.cn: re- 加 place：把它放回原处。

normal.en: Replace with is the phrase for a swap: old out, new in.
normal.cn: replace with 是替换的固定搭配：旧的出去，新的进来。

normal.en: Be replaced by turns the sentence around and puts the newcomer first.
normal.cn: be replaced by 把句子倒过来，让新来者作主语。

normal.en: Replaceable and irreplaceable differ only by the negative prefix.
normal.cn: replaceable 与 irreplaceable 只差一个否定前缀。

normal.en: A replacement part is a part that goes into the same slot.
normal.cn: replacement part 就是装进同一个位置的零件。

abstract.en: Picture a battery sliding out and a fresh one clicking in.
abstract.cn: 想象旧电池滑出，新电池咔哒一声装进去。

abstract.en: Imagine a name plate being unscrewed from an office door.
abstract.cn: 想象办公室门上的名牌被拧下来换掉。

abstract.en: Think of a book returned to the exact gap it left on the shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象一本书被放回书架上原来那个空隙。

examples.en: Please replace the tools when you have finished.
examples.cn: 用完后请把工具放回原处。

examples.en: Robots have replaced many workers on the production line.
examples.cn: 机器人已经取代了生产线上的许多工人。

examples.en: The hospital replaced all the old beds last year.
examples.cn: 医院去年更换了所有旧病床。

dict_mnemonic.text: re-（重新）+ place（位置）＝重新放回位置，进而表示替换；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: re-（重新、再次）+ place（位置，源自拉丁语 platea「宽街、场地」），16 世纪英语内部构成，本义「放回原处」，后引申为「取代、替换」。

sensesIntro.en: One slot is filled again: first the object simply goes back, then it takes over the slot, and finally the old and new are swapped.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个位置被再次填满：先只是把东西放回去，再是它占据这个位置，最后是新旧对换。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty slot filled again by something new or returning.
core.cn: 核心意象：空出的位置被重新填入，或被新物占据。

branches.en: Putting the same object back is the literal re- plus place sense.
branches.cn: 把同一个物件放回去，是 re- 加 place 的字面义。

branches.en: When the newcomer fills the slot, it takes the place of what was there.
branches.cn: 新来者占据位置时，就取代了原本在那里的东西。

branches.en: The slot stays, but the thing inside is deliberately swapped.
branches.cn: 位置不变，但里面的东西被有意换掉。

branches.en: Returning and taking over both depend on the same fixed position.
branches.cn: 放回与接管都依赖同一个固定位置。

branches.en: Substitution and replacement describe the same handover from different angles.
branches.cn: 取代与替换从不同角度描述同一次交接。

intro.en: Replace is an English prefix-and-word formation whose second element comes from Latin through French.
intro.cn: replace 是英语用前缀加单词构成的词，后一部分经法语来自拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin platea gives the idea of a broad place or position, which becomes English place.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 platea 提供「宽阔场地、位置」的意思，后来成为英语 place。

items.exampleCN: re- 出现在 replace 与 restore 开头。

items.example: Place is the base of replace.
items.exampleCN: place 是 replace 的基础词。

items.example: Platea is the distant source of place.
items.exampleCN: platea 是 place 的远源。
replace 由 re- 与 place 合成。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词词尾

items.meaning: the act or thing that replaces

items.example: The prefix ir- makes replaceable negative.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ir- 使 replaceable 变成否定。
词尾 -ible 出现在 irreplaceable 中。

definition_zh: 宏伟的；盛大的；极好的
definition_en: large and impressive in scale, full of ceremony, or very good in informal speech
core_image: 宽阔的石阶通向一座高大的门廊，立柱在阳光下投下长长的影子
scene: 宫殿的台阶通向一扇宏伟的大门。 The palace steps led to a grand entrance.
sceneCN: 这里 grand 是「宏伟的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：宫殿的台阶通向一扇宏伟的大门。

derivatives.zh: 宏伟；壮丽
宏伟地；盛大地
宏大；重大

senses.title: Impressive in scale
senses.definition: large and impressive in size or design
senses.definitionCN: 在规模或设计上宏大而令人印象深刻
senses.example: The palace steps led to a grand entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 宫殿的台阶通向一扇宏伟的大门。
senses.why: This is the central sense of impressive size.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示规模宏伟的核心含义。

senses.title: Full of ceremony
senses.definition: full of ceremony and importance
senses.definitionCN: 充满仪式感与重要性
senses.example: The wedding was a grand affair.
senses.exampleCN: 那场婚礼非常盛大。
senses.why: An event can have the scale of a building.
senses.whyCN: 一场活动也能有建筑的规模。

senses.title: Very good
senses.definition: very good or enjoyable in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示非常好、令人愉快
senses.example: We had a grand day out.
senses.exampleCN: 我们出去玩得很开心。
senses.why: Everyday speech loosened grandeur into simple praise.
senses.whyCN: 日常口语把宏伟松弛成了简单的赞美。

intro.en: Grand came from Latin grandis, great, through Old French.
intro.cn: grand 从拉丁语 grandis（大的）经古法语而来。

items.en: Grandis meant great, full-grown, or mighty.
items.cn: grandis 意为大的、成熟的或强大的。

items.en: Grand meant great and important.
items.cn: grand 意为伟大的、重要的。

items.en: Grand entered English meaning stately and large.
items.cn: grand 以庄严、宏大之义进入英语。

items.en: It described ceremonies and fine buildings.
items.cn: 它用来描述仪式和华美的建筑。

items.en: Informal speech made it a word of praise.
items.cn: 口语使它成为赞美的词。

note.en: Grand is compared with look-alike words and words for magnificence.
note.cn: 把 grand 与形近词以及表示壮丽的词作比较。

a seed
a product name
extremely impressive
impressive to look at
dignified and grand

normalIntro.en: Grand is size and ceremony carried with dignity.
normalIntro.cn: grand 是带着尊严的规模与仪式。

normal.en: The palace steps led to a grand entrance.
normal.cn: 宫殿的台阶通向一扇宏伟的大门。

normal.en: The wedding was a grand affair.

normal.en: The grand total came to two hundred.

abstract.en: Grandeur is scale that asks to be remembered.
abstract.cn: 宏伟，是要求被记住的规模。

abstract.en: A grand plan needs a humble first step.

abstract.en: The grandest rooms are the emptiest at night.
abstract.cn: 最宏伟的房间，夜里最空。

dict_mnemonic.text: grand 来自拉丁语 grandis（大的），表示「宏伟的、盛大的」，口语中也表示「极好的」；grandeur 是「宏伟」，grand entrance 是「宏伟的入口」，grand piano 是「三角钢琴」。

root: 来自拉丁语 grandis（大的、伟大的），经古法语 grand 进入英语，核心义为规模宏大、气象庄严，口语中引申为极好的。

sensesIntro.en: Grand means impressive in scale, full of ceremony, or very good informally.
sensesIntro.cn: grand 指规模宏伟、仪式盛大，或口语中极好的。

core.en: Scale that makes people look up.
core.cn: 让人仰望的规模。

branches.en: Tall pillars frame a wide doorway.
branches.cn: 高高的立柱框出宽阔的门洞。

branches.en: A hall fills with music and ceremony.
branches.cn: 大厅充满音乐与仪式。

branches.en: A family laughs on a long walk.
branches.cn: 一家人长途散步，笑声不断。

branches.en: A building and an event can both make an impression.
branches.cn: 建筑与活动都能留下印象。

branches.en: Ceremony and simple joy both borrow the word.
branches.cn: 仪式与简单的快乐都借用了这个词。

intro.en: Grand forms nouns and adverbs of scale and dignity.
intro.cn: grand 构成表示规模与尊严的名词和副词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is grandis, great or full-grown.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 grandis（大的、成熟的）。

items.example: The palace steps led to a grand entrance.

items.example: We felt the grandness of the old square.

definition_zh: 数据库
definition_en: a large set of information stored in a computer and arranged for quick searching
core_image: 一间排满文件柜、每格都贴着编号的房间
scene: 前台一输入名字，屏幕上立刻跳出档案。 The database found her record in seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 database 指「数据库」（第 1 个义项：有结构地存放数据的系统）；句意是数据库几秒内就找到了她的记录。

derivatives.zh: 数据；资料
资料库

senses.title: An organized store of data
senses.definition: a large body of information arranged so that it can be searched quickly
senses.definitionCN: 按一定方式排列、便于快速检索的大量信息
senses.example: The database found her record in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 数据库几秒内就找到了她的记录。
senses.why: The power lies not in the amount of data but in the order it is kept in.
senses.whyCN: 力量不在数据多少，而在它们被放得多有次序。

senses.title: The software that runs it
senses.definition: the program or system that stores and answers questions about such data
senses.definitionCN: 负责存放数据并回答查询的程序或系统
senses.example: The team installed a new database last month.
senses.exampleCN: 团队上个月装了新的数据库系统。
senses.why: We use one word for the store and for the machine that guards it.
senses.whyCN: 我们用一个词同时指这座仓库和看守它的机器。

intro.en: Database is a modern coinage joining data, the plural of Latin datum, to base, a foundation.
intro.cn: database 是现代的造词，把拉丁语 datum 的复数 data（数据）与 base（基础）拼在一起。

items.en: Datum meant something given, a fact handed over.
items.cn: datum 意为「被给出的东西」，即交出的事实。

items.en: Data entered English as the plural of datum.
items.cn: data 作为 datum 的复数进入英语。

items.en: Data bank named a store of facts kept for later use.
items.cn: data bank 指为日后使用而存放事实的库。

items.en: Database was coined for computer files that could be searched.
items.cn: database 被造出来，指可检索的计算机文件集合。

items.en: Database now covers everything from a phone list to a national registry.
items.cn: 如今 database 从电话簿一直指到国家登记系统。

note.en: The look-alike group breaks the compound into its parts, and the meaning group names other collections of records.
note.cn: 形近组把这个复合词拆成部件，近义组则列出其他形式的记录集合。

entries.definition: facts and figures collected for use
entries.definitionCN: 为使用而收集的事实与数字

entries.definition: the bottom or starting point of something
a large store of information
a store of old records kept for reference
entries.definitionCN: 为查考而保存旧记录的地方

entries.definition: an official list kept in order
a book of records kept in rows

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a wall of numbered drawers and end with an answer appearing in a second.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一面编号抽屉的墙开始，落到一秒内跳出来的答案。

normal.en: A database is a library where no book is out of place.
normal.cn: 数据库是一座没有一本书放错位置的图书馆。

normal.en: Order is the only thing that makes a million facts useful.
normal.cn: 让一百万条事实变得有用的，只有次序。

normal.en: The word joins what is given to the ground it stands on.
normal.cn: 这个词把「被给出的东西」接到了「它立足的地基」上。

normal.en: A question asked well is already half an answer.
normal.cn: 问得好的问题，已经是一半的答案。

normal.en: Every record is a person who once filled in a form.
normal.cn: 每条记录背后，都是一个曾经填过表的人。

abstract.en: Picture a long room of grey cabinets with small labels.
abstract.cn: 想象一间长屋子，摆满贴着小标签的灰色柜子。

abstract.en: Picture a cursor blinking beside an empty search box.
abstract.cn: 想象一个空搜索框旁闪烁的光标。

abstract.en: Picture one line of text rising to the top of a screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一行字升到屏幕最上方。

examples.en: The database found her record in seconds.
examples.cn: 数据库几秒内就找到了她的记录。

examples.en: All the patient records are kept in one database.
examples.cn: 所有病人记录都存在同一个数据库里。

examples.en: They built a database of local plant names.
examples.cn: 他们建了一个本地植物名称的数据库。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 database 记成「数据基地」：data 是数据，base 是基地，数据存放的基地就是数据库。

root: 由 data（数据，拉丁语 datum「被给出之物」的复数）与 base（基础、基地）复合而成，二十世纪六十年代随计算机检索系统出现，指按结构存放、便于查询的大量信息。

sensesIntro.en: From the ordered store of facts, to the system that keeps answering for it.
sensesIntro.cn: 从按序存放的事实，到替它回答问题的系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a room of numbered drawers, each holding one kind of fact.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间编了号的抽屉房，每格装着一种事实。

branches.en: The first sense is the store itself, judged by its order.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是仓库本身，以次序论高低。

branches.en: The second sense is the machine that reads and answers.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是负责读取和回答的机器。

branches.en: The store and the system are named together because neither works alone.
branches.cn: 仓库与系统合称，因为缺了谁都不成。

branches.en: A drawer never answers; the index does.
branches.cn: 抽屉从不回答，回答的是索引。

branches.en: The system is only as good as the order it inherited.
branches.cn: 系统的水平，取决于它继承下来的那套次序。

intro.en: Database is a compound, so its family is built by joining data and base to other words.
intro.cn: database 是个复合词，它的一族靠把 data 与 base 同别的词拼起来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin element is datum, something given; base is Greek in origin, a step or foundation.
latinIntro.cn: 其中的拉丁成分是 datum（被给出之物）；base 源自希腊语，意为台阶或基础。

items.example: The hospital keeps a databank of scans.
items.exampleCN: 医院存有一个扫描资料库。

items.meaning: software for storing and searching data
the work of keeping a database in order
a database reached through a network
items.example: The journal is in an online database.
items.exampleCN: 这份期刊在一个在线数据库里。

items.meaning: a person who looks after a database
items.example: Only the database administrator can change it.
items.exampleCN: 只有数据库管理员能改动它。

latinEntries.example: Datum is the singular behind data.
latinEntries.exampleCN: datum 是 data 背后的单数形式。

definition_zh: 批评；指责；评论
definition_en: to say what is wrong with someone or something, or to judge a work
core_image: 有人指着报表上的漏洞，一条条说下去
scene: 会议上有人指着报表上的漏洞，一条条说下去。 They began to criticize the plan before it was finished.
sceneCN: 这里 criticize 指「批评」（第 1 个义项：指出某人或某事的缺点）；句意是计划还没做完，他们就开始批评了。

derivatives.zh: 批评
评论家
批评的；关键的
评论文章

senses.title: Point out faults
senses.definition: to say what is wrong with a person, a plan or an action
senses.definitionCN: 指出某人、某项计划或某个行为哪里不对
senses.example: The report criticizes the long delay.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告批评了长期的拖延。
senses.why: A fault is easier to fix once it is named aloud.
senses.whyCN: 毛病被说出口，才更容易修。

senses.title: Judge a work in public
senses.definition: to judge the merits and faults of a work for the public
senses.definitionCN: 面向公众评判作品的优点与缺点
senses.example: He criticizes films for a weekly magazine.
senses.exampleCN: 他为一家周刊写影评。
senses.why: A person paid to judge must say both what fails and what works.
senses.whyCN: 靠评判吃饭的人，得同时说出哪里失败、哪里成立。

intro.en: Criticize joins critic, from Greek kritikos, with the verb suffix -ize.
intro.cn: criticize 由 critic（源自希腊语 kritikos）加动词后缀 -ize 构成。

items.en: Krinein meant to separate and to judge.
items.cn: krinein 意为分开与判断。

items.en: Kritikos described a person able to judge.
items.cn: kritikos 形容有能力判断的人。

items.en: Critic named a judge of literature.
items.cn: critic 指文学评判者。

items.en: Criticize meant to act as a critic.
items.cn: criticize 意为像评论家那样行事。

items.en: It took on the sense of finding faults.
items.cn: 它多了指出缺点的意思。

items.en: It covers both blame and public judgement.
items.cn: 它兼指责备与公开评判。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the critic- stem, and the meaning group names other ways of speaking against something.
note.cn: 形近组共享 critic- 词干，近义组列出其他表示责难的说法。

entries.definition: a person who judges works
the act of judging faults
judging, or extremely important
to say someone is responsible for a fault
to say strongly that something is wrong
to point out a small mistake

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a finger on a report and end with a magazine page.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从指在报表上的一根手指，走到杂志的一页。

normal.en: Critic plus -ize: to do what a critic does.
normal.cn: critic 加 -ize：去做评论家做的事。

normal.en: A finger on a fault is faster than a pen on a plan.
normal.cn: 手指点毛病，比笔改计划快得多。

normal.en: Criticize the work, not the person.
normal.cn: 批评那件事，别批评那个人。

normal.en: Say it once, clearly, then offer a way to fix it.
normal.cn: 说一次，说清楚，再给出修的办法。

normal.en: Praise and blame leave by the same door.
normal.cn: 称赞和责备，走的是同一扇门。

abstract.en: Picture a row of red circles on a chart.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上一排红圈。

abstract.en: Picture a raised hand in a meeting.
abstract.cn: 想象会上举起的一只手。

abstract.en: Picture a printed page with one harsh line.
abstract.cn: 想象印出来的一页上有一句狠话。

examples.en: They criticized the plan for being too slow.
examples.cn: 他们批评这项计划太慢。

examples.en: She criticizes films for a small magazine.
examples.cn: 她为一家小杂志写影评。

examples.en: He was criticized for saying too little.
examples.cn: 他因说得太少而受到批评。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 criticize 记成 critic（评论家）加 -ize（做）：去做评论家做的事，就是评判与挑毛病。

root: 由 critic（源自希腊语 kritikos，善于判断的）加动词后缀 -ize 构成；本义是「像评论家那样评判」，后专指指出缺点、加以责备。

sensesIntro.en: From naming a fault to judging a work before the public.
sensesIntro.cn: 从指出一处毛病，到当众评判一部作品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger pointing at a flaw in a report.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指点在报表的漏洞上。

branches.en: The first act is to name what went wrong.
branches.cn: 第一步，是说出哪里出了错。

branches.en: The second is to weigh the whole work in public.
branches.cn: 第二步，是当众掂量整部作品。

branches.en: Both senses share the same judging hand.
branches.cn: 两个义项共用同一只评判的手。

branches.en: A blamed person may still repair the fault.
branches.cn: 被批评的人，仍有机会把毛病修好。

branches.en: A public judgement must also name what works.
branches.cn: 公开的评判也得说出哪里成立。

intro.en: Criticize adds the verb suffix -ize to critic, a word of Greek origin.
intro.cn: criticize 在 critic 后加动词后缀 -ize，而 critic 源自希腊语。

latinIntro.en: The stem crit- goes back through Latin criticus to Greek krinein, to judge.
latinIntro.cn: 词干 crit- 经拉丁语 criticus 上溯到希腊语 krinein（判断）。

items.exampleCN: 他给了一个带评判的答复。

items.example: The critique was two pages long.
Apply one criterion at a time.

latinEntries.example: Latin criticus named the judge of books.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 criticus 指评判书籍的人。
